SUN.exemption_authority: 'Policy Exemptions: No exemptions apply to this Policy.' The only relief routes are the Section 3 Exempt Dealing categories and a Section 8 waiver for Exceptional Circumstances, granted by the Suncorp Chairman (Directors), the Audit Committee Chairman (the Chairman) or the Group CEO (other Prescribed Persons), each acting through the Company Secretary. No one has power to waive the section 5.1 hedging ban or the section 5.2 short-term dealing and short selling bans, which are not expressed as Closed Period restrictions and so fall outside the waiver mechanism.
jurisdiction_overlays: ASX Listing Rule 12.10 (the policy is lodged under it) and Listing Rule notification of Directors' interests, which is the stated reason for the three business day post-trade notification
Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) insider trading provisions
Suncorp has an ADR programme (ADR: SNMCY) but the policy imposes no US-specific overlay

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is drafted around 'holdings in Suncorp Securities' generally rather than plan or unvested securities, so a put and call collar over vested unrestricted shares is prohibited outright, and 'including unvested performance rights' reads as an extension of that scope rather than a limit on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no waiver for the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Policy Exemptions: No exemptions apply to this Policy. The Section 8 waiver enables Prescribed Persons 'to Deal in Suncorp Securities during Closed Periods' in Exceptional Circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The waiver power is confined to lifting Closed Period restrictions, so there is no mechanism by which the Chairman, Group CEO or Board could authorise a collar despite section 5.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Suncorp Chairman, or the Group CEO, will review any request for waiver or clearance to Deal by Prescribed Persons or their Connected Persons which involves entering into a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is permitted in principle subject to individual approval by the Chairman or Group CEO who may attach conditions, so the financing is not the obstacle here; the hedging ban on the derivative legs is.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale is an exempt dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: involuntary disposal under a margin loan: a disposal of Suncorp Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually favourable for a lender: enforcement or margin-call sale by the bank is expressly exempt from Closed Period restrictions and from the clearance requirement, so the bank's security can be realised at any time without putting the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: granting security is itself a dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Examples of Dealing in Securities include: ... granting a mortgage, lien, charge or other security interest (such as a Margin Loan) over Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Executing the security document over the collared shares is a Dealing in its own right, so it needs prior written clearance, must be outside Closed Periods and must be completed inside the clearance window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Security or Securities: ... derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities, whether or not the securities or the derivative products are issued or created by Suncorp or by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and the call written by a bank are themselves Suncorp Securities, so every leg, roll, amendment and settlement is a separate Dealing subject to clearance and Closed Periods even before section 5.1 is considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-Term Dealing ... means buying and selling the same Security within a six month period and entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban did not apply, a forward-settled or short-dated collar is the express example of prohibited short-term Dealing, so any structure would need a tenor comfortably beyond six months and no early unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance request to Deal can be given, refused or withdrawn by Suncorp in its discretion, without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the person seeking clearance. If clearance to Deal is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be withdrawn after it is given and before execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a trade cannot proceed, so pricing and mandate documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In certain circumstances the Company Secretary may be asked to restrict individuals from Dealing in Suncorp Securities who may be in possession of Price Sensitive Information for a period of time ('Restricted List').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An individual can be blocked from dealing at any time outside the scheduled Closed Periods, which would prevent entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement of any structure without notice to the counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Connected Person of a Prescribed Person includes ... a company, trust or entity that the Prescribed Person (or any of their family members falling within any of the above categories) controls or has an interest in.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company does not escape either the hedging ban or the clearance and Closed Period regime, and the 'has an interest in' limb is wider than control.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban has the widest personal scope
bespoke_clauses.clause: 5.1 Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is addressed to all Directors, Employees and Contractors rather than only to Prescribed Persons, so it catches executives well below KMP level who are otherwise free of Closed Periods and clearance.

SUN.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy, and the obstacle is the hedging ban rather than the financing. Section 5.1 prohibits all Suncorp Directors, Employees and Contractors from entering any hedging transaction designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, and that ban is drafted around holdings generally, with unvested performance rights expressly swept in, so a purchased put and written call over vested unrestricted shares is caught; there is no clearance, waiver or exemption route out of it, because the Section 8 Exceptional Circumstances waiver only lifts Closed Period restrictions and the policy states that no exemptions apply. By contrast the loan leg would be workable in isolation: granting a mortgage, lien or charge over Suncorp Securities is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance, section 6 expressly contemplates a new or increased Margin Loan or 'other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction' subject to personal review by the Suncorp Chairman or Group CEO who may impose any terms they see fit, and an involuntary disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is an Exempt Dealing that can occur even in a Closed Period. If the hedging ban were ever amended, a structure would still need clearance for each leg from the Chairman (Directors) or Group CEO (other Prescribed Persons), execution within a specified period of no more than five business days, entry outside the 1 January, 1 July and pre-AGM Closed Periods and off the Restricted List, notification to the Company Secretary within three business days for Directors and ELT members, and a tenor beyond six months to avoid the short-term dealing ban on forward contracts.

tiers.name: Scentre Group Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: Everyone the policy applies to: all Scentre Group Directors and the officers and employees of Scentre Group Limited, Scentre Group Trusts 1, 2 and 3 and their controlled entities. Subject to the Insider Trading Prohibition at all times, but not to blackout periods, clearance, the margin lending ban, the short selling ban or the short-term trading ban, which bite only on Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Specified Persons, Designated Persons, and employees who are likely to have access to confidential information of a 'market sensitive' nature in the ordinary course of their employment. This is the tier that carries the substantive restrictions: no trading in blackout periods, clearance to trade outside them, no margin lending, no short selling, no short-term or speculative trading, and prior Company Secretary approval for other security arrangements over Scentre Group Securities.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: A Scentre Group Director, any executive named as key management personnel in the Group's remuneration report, any Company Secretary, and any other person classified as a Specified Person by the Clearance Committee. Distinguished by clearance from the Clearance Committee (the Chair of the Board and the Chair of the Audit Committee) rather than the CEO.

Used only in section 9(f): for KMP, the excluded-trading carve-out for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights does not extend to enforcement under a margin lending arrangement.

The Restricted Person must inform them, communicate with the Clearance Officer for them, and ensure their compliance.

SCG.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may extend a blackout period or specify any additional period as a blackout period. Separately, the Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions on certain employees at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered by employees directly involved in or with knowledge of those matters. The policy does not say either is announced, and a person refused clearance must keep the refusal confidential.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and other Financial Products issued over Scentre Group Securities and able to be traded on a financial market are themselves Scentre Group Securities, so trading them requires prior written clearance and is barred in blackout periods. Any such derivative must not be short-term or speculative under 11(d), and clearance will be refused if the request rests on short-term or speculative considerations.
rules.evidence: any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: A bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is arguably outside limb (d) of Scentre Group Securities, which is confined to Financial Products 'able to be traded on a financial market', so the clearance and blackout machinery may not reach it on its own terms. But 11(d) expressly regulates 'derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities' without that market-traded limitation, and Financial Product expressly includes options, forward contracts and swaps. The prudent and evidently intended reading is that an OTC collar is caught and needs clearance; it is prohibited if short-term or speculative.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans are prohibited from hedging unvested awards. The operative detail sits in a separate document, the Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy, which is not part of this policy and must be obtained separately.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards ... These prohibitions are outlined in the Scentre Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.

rules.detail: The ban is expressly extended past vesting: awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or are otherwise subject to deferral of delivery cannot be hedged. This closes the usual gap between vesting and release for plan securities.
rules.evidence: hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery offered under the equity-linked incentive plans operated by Scentre Group.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is carefully bounded: it reaches unvested awards and vested awards still in a holding lock or subject to deferred delivery, and stops there. Shares that have vested and been released, and ordinary on-market holdings, are not covered by any hedging ban in this policy. Hedging them is regulated only as trading: prior written clearance from the relevant Clearance Officer, outside blackout periods, not short-term or speculative, and subject to whatever the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy says.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan over released shares is a transaction associated with disposing of or agreeing to dispose of Scentre Group Securities and so is a trade requiring prior written clearance; the secured loan leg additionally needs the Company Secretary's prior approval under 11(b). It must not be short-term (under three months) or speculative.
rules.evidence: “deal” or “trade” includes to take part in any transaction associated with buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, converting or agreeing to do any of those things

rules.detail: Flat ban with no definition, no carve-out and no clearance route. Because it is undefined, a physically settled short leg or a cash-settled position taken without holding the underlying could be characterised as short selling.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short selling of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is nowhere named, is not listed in the definition of deal or trade, and is not among the excluded dealings. A title-transfer stock loan would involve a disposal and so be a trade, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for difference are expressly named as Financial Products, and 11(d) regulates derivative and other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities. A CFD is therefore permitted only with prior written clearance and only if not short-term (under three months) or speculative, which in practice will bar most CFD positions; a short CFD would also engage the short selling ban.

rules.detail: Flat ban on entering margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities, with no clearance or waiver route. The ban is confined to 'all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements'; the Company Secretary is the arbiter of whether a given arrangement is a margin loan or merely a security arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Scentre Group Securities is not a 'trade' under the deal/trade definition and is not caught by the margin lending ban, but the policy imposes a standalone requirement of prior approval from the Company Secretary before entering into any such security arrangement. rules.detail: The policy draws an express and unusual line: the ban stops at margin lending and does not extend to other types of loan secured by a security interest over Scentre Group Securities. A term loan from a bank secured on collared shares is therefore permitted, conditional on prior approval from the Company Secretary, who is also the person to consult on whether the facility is properly classified as margin lending.
rules.evidence: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

SCG.exemption_authority: No general exemption power. The only relief from blackout periods is an exceptional circumstances notice under section 6, which can be issued only by a Clearance Officer (the Clearance Committee for Specified Persons, the CEO for Designated Persons, the CFO or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons), only to a person not holding unpublished market sensitive information, only for severe financial hardship, a court order or court enforceable undertaking or other exceptional circumstances, and only in respect of a sale, not a purchase. Clearance Officers are told to exercise the discretion with caution if in any doubt, and Scentre Group may have to notify the nature of the exceptional circumstances to ASX. No one is given power to waive the margin lending, short selling or short-term trading prohibitions in section 11.
jurisdiction_overlays: ASX Listing Rule 12.10 (lodgement), Listing Rule 3.19A (Director interest notices) and Listing Rules 3.1 / 3.1A (basis for the CEO's ad hoc restrictions)

Stapled structure: the policy covers Scentre Group stapled securities and, separately, units in the Carindale Property Trust, each with its own blackout calendar

bespoke_clauses.clause: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities. However, if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that makes a funded collar feasible: a bank term loan secured on the collared securities is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs only the Company Secretary's prior approval, so the financing leg has a defined, single-approver route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person should also consult with the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement is properly classified as a margin lending or security arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretary decides whether the facility is 'properly described as' margin lending, so the loan should be documented with no LVR-based margin call or top-up mechanics and the characterisation confirmed in writing before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank under a non-margin secured facility is excluded from the blackout and trading restrictions even for directors and KMP, so the bank's security can be realised in a blackout period without putting the executive in breach; the carve-back bites only on margin lending, which is prohibited anyway.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban is bounded to plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no hedging prohibition on vested, released or ordinarily acquired securities, so a collar over unrestricted shares is not barred by this policy, but shares still in a holding lock or subject to deferred delivery must be excluded from the collar pool.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging rules sit outside this policy
bespoke_clauses.clause: These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The operative hedging restrictions are in a separate document not lodged with this policy, so that policy must be reviewed before any collar is priced; it may be wider than the summary given here.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban expressly reaches derivatives over the securities, so a collar must have a tenor of at least three months and should not contain early unwind or knock-out features that would make it short-term in substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance to trade will not be given where the request to trade is based on considerations of a short-term or speculative nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance application should present the collar as long-term risk management of a concentrated holding rather than a view on the price, since the Clearance Officer must refuse anything framed as short-term or speculative.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC products may fall outside the Securities definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Scentre Group Securities means ... any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bilateral OTC collar may not be 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so may sit outside the clearance and blackout machinery on the literal wording, but section 11(d) regulates derivatives over the securities without that limit, so clearance should be sought regardless rather than relying on the gap.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or if there is a change in circumstances ... must complete the trade within three business days of the clearance being received, and fresh approval must be sought for any trades after this clearance period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within three business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled before execution, so the bank's mandate should contemplate silent withdrawal and re-approval for any roll or restructure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if the clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why the trade cannot proceed, so documentation should not require a reason to be given for withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.topic: brokers with discretion must be notified
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must also inform their brokers or financial advisers who have discretion to trade on their behalf that the Restricted Person is restricted from trading Scentre Group Securities under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If any part of the structure gives the bank discretionary dealing authority over the securities, the bank must be formally notified of the trading restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other entity (including family companies, family trusts and personal superannuation funds) over which the Restricted Person or Restricted Person's immediate family member has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence (including in its capacity as trustee or shareholder or unitholder)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust, SMSF or personal company does not avoid clearance, the blackout periods or the section 11 prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions on certain employees at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll or unwind can be blocked at any time outside the scheduled blackout calendar and without public notice, so execution timing cannot be guaranteed to the counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A blackout period is: (a) in respect of stapled securities of Scentre Group: the period commencing on 1 July ... and the period commencing on 1 January ...; and (b) in respect of units in the Carindale Property Trust: ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Scentre Group stapled securities are effectively closed from 1 January and 1 July until two hours after the relevant results release, leaving only narrow open windows in which a collar can be entered, amended or unwound.

SCG.summary: A funded collar over vested, released Scentre Group stapled securities is possible under this policy, and it is one of the more accommodating policies for the structure. There is no general hedging ban: section 10(b) prohibits hedging only of unvested awards and of awards that have vested but remain in a holding lock or subject to deferral of delivery, so unrestricted holdings are outside it, although the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy must be reviewed because the operative prohibitions live there. Critically, section 11(b) confines the margin lending ban to arrangements properly described as margin lending and expressly permits other loan arrangements secured by a security interest over Scentre Group Securities, subject only to the prior approval of the Company Secretary, and section 9(f) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights as excluded trading even for Key Management Personnel, with the carve-back applying only to margin lending. The conditions are that the derivative legs and any share disposal need prior written clearance from the Clearance Committee (Specified Persons, including Directors and KMP) or the CEO (Designated Persons), must be executed within three business days of clearance and outside the 1 January and 1 July blackout periods and any Board or CEO ad hoc restriction, must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days (and in time for a Listing Rule 3.19A notice for Directors), and the facility must be documented so that it is not a margin loan and the collar has a tenor of at least three months and is not presented as short-term or speculative, since clearance must be refused on that ground.

rules.detail: No express derivatives prohibition. PME Securities expressly include any derivative of PME shares or securities, naming equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not; to apply for, acquire, convert or dispose of one (or agree to do so) is a Dealing. An OTC put and written call therefore require the section 8.b) pre-dealing notification and Company Secretary confirmation, must fall in a Trading Window (or have Chairman approval), and are barred in Blackout Periods and while holding Inside Information.

rules.detail: The policy contains no hedging prohibition and no definition of hedging or of limiting economic risk. 'Hedges' appear only as a category of PME Securities, so entering a hedge is a Dealing subject to the ordinary window and clearance machinery. No distinction is drawn between vested, unvested or restricted plan securities; section 12 defers to the rules of the Pro Medicus Share Plan and Option Plan, which are not part of this document and may impose their own hedging ban.

A collar or prepaid forward is a derivative of PME Securities and an agreement to dispose, so it is a Dealing requiring the pre-dealing notification, no Inside Information confirmation, Company Secretary clearance and execution within 7 days, inside a Trading Window.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives of PME shares settled by cash, so they fall within PME Securities and dealing in them requires the section 8.b) clearance and a Trading Window. No speculative or short-term trading ban exists to catch them separately.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no prohibition on hedging, margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling or short-term dealing; the only reference to financing is the post-dealing disclosure of 'any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is not banned, so the structure turns entirely on window timing, Company Secretary clearance and disclosure rather than on any substantive prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PME Securities include any derivatives of PME shares and securities (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs, cash-settled or physically settled, are PME Securities, so each of entry, roll, unwind and settlement is a separate Dealing needing its own clearance and window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing is generally confined to three 30-day Trading Windows: after the full-year results, after the half-year results and after the AGM.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There are only about 90 dealing days a year, and the Chairman can shorten any window, so collar execution and any unwind must be scheduled tightly against the results and AGM calendar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Dealing must occur within 7 days of being so advised (and within 7 days of approval where the Chairman has approved an out-of-window Dealing).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete inside a 7-day clearance life or the clearance must be re-obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Dealing ... must comply with any conditions (including disclosure) which may be imposed by the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman, the Board). Any approval given or conditions imposed are within the discretion of the Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach open-ended conditions, including public disclosure of the collar, as the price of any out-of-window execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ad hoc blackouts and window truncation
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman can, as he or she deems appropriate, reduce the period of any Trading Window from time to time ... the Board or Chairman may, from time to time, declare any other period to be a 'Blackout Period'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar unwind, roll or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice by a declared Blackout Period or a truncated window, so the documentation needs cash settlement or deferral mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees who acquire PME Securities under the Pro Medicus Share Plan, Pro Medicus Option Plan or any other employee incentive scheme from time to time must also comply with the rules of that Plan when Dealing in those securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging and encumbrance bans over unvested or plan-held shares may sit in the plan rules, which are not in this policy and must be diligenced separately before collaring plan shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to all PME Directors and PME Employees. There is no definition of associates, and no extension to spouses, dependants, controlled entities or trusts.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On its face the policy does not reach a family trust or controlled company holding the shares, though the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition and directors' notifiable interest obligations still bite.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Strict compliance with this policy is a condition of employment. Breaches of this policy will be subject to disciplinary action, which may include termination of employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale in a Blackout Period would be an unapproved Dealing by the borrower with dismissal risk, even though the policy is silent on forced sales.

PME.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2011 insider-trading document with no substantive prohibitions on hedging, derivatives, margin lending or secured financing. Both collar legs are PME Securities because the definition expressly captures equity swaps, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not, so entering, rolling, unwinding and settling the collar are each Dealings that require prior written notice of intention to the Company Secretary, a written confirmation of no Inside Information, and advice from the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the Dealing, with execution inside 7 days. Dealings must fall within one of the three 30-day Trading Windows after the full-year results, half-year results and AGM, outside the two four-week Blackout Periods and any ad hoc Blackout the Board or Chairman declares, and the Chairman may shorten a window or bar an individual; out-of-window execution needs the Chairman's (or for the Chairman, the Board's) approval on exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, subject to any conditions including disclosure. The secured loan is not itself a Dealing and is not prohibited, but full details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting the shares must be reported in writing to the Company Secretary after the Dealing, and directors must also meet their notifiable interest obligations and their letter agreement with the company. The main residual risks are the narrow dealing calendar with no forced-sale carve-out, and the rules of the Pro Medicus Share and Option Plans, which are incorporated by reference and may impose hedging or encumbrance restrictions on plan shares that this policy does not.

rules.section: 9-10, 14; Definitions (Securities, Dealing in/Trading in IAG Securities)
rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule. Securities expressly include financial products such as warrants, options, contracts for difference and other derivatives relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, IAG securities, whether or not created by IAG or a third party, so there is no venue or issuer limit. Applying for, acquiring or disposing of such a product, or entering into an agreement to do so, is a Dealing and needs a Trading Consent Request approved in a Trading Window, no Inside Information, and satisfaction of the front page test.
rules.evidence: financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by IAG Group or third parties.

rules.detail: For those who are not Specified Persons the only constraints on dealing in an IAG derivative are the Inside Information prohibition and the front page test; there is no Trading Window, consent or record-keeping requirement, and the margin lending prohibition in clause 34 does not reach them.
rules.evidence: This Policy prohibits you and your Closely Related Parties from Dealing in IAG Securities where you or they are in possession of Inside Information.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on hedging plan securities before vesting; it applies to any participant in an IAG employee, executive or director equity plan, not only Specified Persons, and extends to Closely Related Parties of Specified Persons. Hedging is defined broadly as any arrangement operating to limit economic risk associated with holding IAG Securities, so a purchased put over unvested rights is caught. No approval route exists.
rules.evidence: IAG Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG by any participant must never be hedged prior to vesting. This requirement also extends to Closely Related Parties of Specified Persons.

rules.detail: Vested shares that remain subject to a holding lock or a restriction on dealing under an IAG plan may never be hedged. This is a separate, absolute prohibition from the pre-vesting ban and again has no consent or exception route, so disposal restriction periods must have fully expired before any collar is placed over plan shares.
rules.evidence: IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is confined to plan securities that are unvested or under a holding lock, so hedging fully vested unrestricted shares (or shares acquired on market) is not banned. It is, however, a Dealing in Securities because instruments that operate to limit economic risk are themselves Securities, so it needs prior consent, a Trading Window, no Inside Information and satisfaction of the front page test, and any funding leg secured on the shares would separately breach clause 34.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding IAG Securities.

rules.detail: For a plan participant who is not a Specified Person, hedging vested, unlocked IAG securities is not prohibited and no consent or window applies; only the Inside Information prohibition and the front page test bite.
rules.evidence: IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named, but any monetisation that uses IAG Securities as collateral, including a loan secured on collared shares, is caught by the blanket prohibition on using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction. A monetisation with no collateral element (for example a cash-settled hedge over vested unrestricted shares with an unsecured loan) is only a Dealing requiring consent in a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and is not listed in the Dealing definition; only the Inside Information prohibition, the front page test and, for Specified Persons, the window, consent and three-month short-term trading rules would apply to any sale.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the Dealing definition (apply for, acquire or dispose of, or agree to do so). Depending on structure it could be characterised as a disposal, and a lend that secures a financing would be caught by the clause 34 collateral prohibition, but the Policy is silent.

Contracts for difference are expressly named as a category of Securities rather than in a prohibition, so dealing in one is a Dealing requiring consent within a Trading Window. In practice the three-month short-term trading ban in clause 30 and the front page test would defeat most CFD positions.
rules.evidence: financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities

rules.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities, and transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account, are both expressly prohibited for Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties. This prohibition was added by the 30 November 2023 amendment. There is no vesting-state carve-out, no grandfathering language for pre-existing arrangements, and no approval or exemption route.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by: a. entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities; or b. transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Clause 34 is located in the 'Other Restrictions' section that applies to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties only; the Policy imposes no margin lending restriction on other Directors, Employees or Contractors.

Granting security is not itself within the Dealing definition, but clause 34 prohibits the use of IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, which captures a mortgage, charge, pledge or security interest over IAG shares given to any financier, not just a margin lender. The two limbs that follow are expressly non-exhaustive examples.
rules.evidence: must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by:

rules.detail: No encumbrance restriction applies to Directors, Employees or Contractors who are not Specified Persons, and granting security is not a Dealing under the definition.

The prohibition is drafted at the level of collateral in 'any financial transaction', so it is broader than margin lending and covers a bank loan secured on collared shares, a limited recourse loan, a securities-backed lending facility and a prepaid forward supported by a share pledge. No approver may consent to it; the Exceptional Circumstances route in clauses 19 to 23 relieves only the Trading Window requirement, not clause 34.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: The Policy says nothing about secured financing by Directors, Employees or Contractors who are not Specified Persons.

A flat three-month gap is required between a purchase and a sale of any IAG Securities by a Specified Person or their Closely Related Party. No carve-outs are stated for plan vesting, DRP acquisitions or exercise of rights, although the clause 27 exclusions take those dealings outside the Policy generally. Because derivatives are Securities, a collar with a tenor or unwind inside three months of any acquisition is exposed to this ban.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.

rules.detail: The no-speculative-trading rule is confined to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties.

IAG.exemption_authority: The IAG Board Chair (the IAG Board Audit Committee Chair where the request is from the Chair) may consent to a Specified Person Dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances, on evidence, if the trade is the most reasonable course of action available and the person holds no Inside Information and satisfies the front page test; the trade must be completed within 5 business days unless otherwise specified. That relief goes only to the Trading Window requirement. No officer has power to waive the hedging prohibitions in clauses 32 and 33, the margin lending and collateral prohibition in clause 34 or the three-month short-term trading ban in clause 30; only the IAG Board can change the Policy itself (the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary may make minor administrative changes and approve changes to the Specified Persons list).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by: a. entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities; or b. transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is squarely prohibited for every Specified Person and their Closely Related Parties, with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, so the structure cannot be offered to this population as designed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition is on collateral in 'any financial transaction'; the margin lending and margin account limbs are introduced by 'including by', so they are examples rather than the limit.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Recharacterising the facility as a securities-backed loan, a limited recourse loan or a pledged prepaid forward does not escape clause 34.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means ... financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by IAG Group or third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs written by a bank are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll, exercise, unwind and settlement are each separate Dealings requiring their own consent within a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IAG Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG by any participant must never be hedged prior to vesting ... IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an unfunded collar can only be placed over plan shares that have vested and are free of any holding lock, and the ban reaches Closely Related Parties so a family trust holding cannot be used.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings involving conditional orders must be placed and executed during a Trading Window (e.g., a specified, minimum sell or maximum purchase price or a stop-loss instruction).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any price-triggered feature of a collar - a knock-in or knock-out barrier, automatic unwind or stop-loss - must both trigger and complete inside a Trading Window, which is impractical for a multi-year structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where consent is required for a trade under this Policy, consent will not be granted where the approver does not consider that the trade would satisfy the front page test. This decision of the approver is final.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over an executive's shareholding is precisely the kind of trade that may be judged to look inappropriate on the front page, and the approver's refusal is final, unreasoned and confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent may be withdrawn if new information is revealed or there is a change in circumstances, and that decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the Specified Person seeking consent and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on consent surviving to signing or settlement, and the executive cannot explain a withdrawal to the counterparty because it must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consents to trade ... will be effective for 5 business days (but no later than the last day of the Trading Window), unless a different timeframe is specified in the consent provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the derivative legs must complete within 5 business days and before the window closes, so documentation must be fully negotiated before consent is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because derivatives are Securities with no stated carve-outs, a collar's purchased put and written call and any unwind must be spaced more than three months from related purchases and sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of notification, as the IAG Board may vary, suspend or terminate (conditionally or unconditionally) Trading Windows arrangements at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution and unwind dates cannot be committed in advance, since the Board can close a window at any time and the only relief is a discretionary Exceptional Circumstances consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clause 14's table routes consent requests from Non-Executive Directors of a Specified Board (excluding the IAG Board Chair) to the 'GCEO and Group General Counsel & Company Secretary', while the clause 36 roles table gives the IAG Board Chair responsibility to approve trading by other Non-Executive Directors, the GCEO and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a director-level collar the correct approver is ambiguous on the face of the Policy, so the bank should require evidence of consent from both the Chair and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls, lender enforcement and pre-existing financing arrangements; there is no grandfathering wording accompanying the clause 34 prohibition added in the 30 November 2023 amendment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out permitting a secured lender to sell during a closed period, and no stated transition for legacy secured facilities, so any existing arrangement is exposed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Mandatory Holdings means the minimum holding of IAG ordinary shares required to be attained by IAG Directors and by the GCEO and GLT, in accordance with IAG's Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The separate Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy may require an unhedged minimum holding and must be diligenced, as this Policy neither operationalises nor excludes hedged shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IAG Directors who undertake a Dealing in IAG Securities following consent must provide the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day of the execution of the trade a confirmation of trade so that an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's collar would become publicly disclosed on an Appendix 3Y within days of execution, which feeds back into the front page test at the consent stage.

IAG.summary: A funded collar is not possible for IAG Specified Persons, the population that includes the directors and executives a bank would target. Clause 34, added by the 30 November 2023 amendment, prohibits Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties from using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, with margin lending and transfers into a margin account given only as examples, and no approver has power to waive it. The derivative legs alone are also constrained: instruments that limit economic risk are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trading Consent Request approved by the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary (or, for Non-Executive Directors, the more senior approver route), inside one of the three roughly 20 business day Trading Windows, valid for only 5 business days, subject to the front page test whose refusal is final and confidential, and subject to the three-month short-term trading ban. Plan shares can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, so only fully vested unrestricted shares are candidates, and any price-triggered or conditional feature must be both placed and executed within a window. A collar could in principle be offered on an unsecured basis over vested unrestricted shares, and Directors, Employees and Contractors who are not Specified Persons are not caught by clauses 30 or 34 at all, but for the target population the funded structure is barred.

PLS.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The umbrella class to whom the whole policy applies: Key Management Personnel (including any director, executive or otherwise), nominated Employees and contractors, and Connected Persons of both. All substantive prohibitions (Blackout Periods, Additional Periods, hedging, margin loans and other secured lending, short term or speculative trading, non-discretionary trading plans) apply to this class without differentiation; only the identity of the Approving Officer differs.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director (whether executive or otherwise). Distinguished only for clearance (Chair, or in his/her absence the Managing Director).

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: An employee or contractor of the Group nominated by the Managing Director or Company Secretary from time to time as a person to whom the Policy applies. Distinguished only for clearance (Managing Director, or in his/her absence the Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director in his or her own personal dealing capacity; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board in his or her own personal dealing capacity; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, a parent, an unlisted body corporate which the KMP or Employee controls or is a director of, a trust of which the KMP or Employee is a trustee and of which he or she or any of those persons is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the KMP or Employee has significant influence or control. The KMP or Employee must procure the Connected Person to comply.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule, but Company Securities expressly include derivatives of shares and rights, naming hedges and over-the-counter options, cash-settled or otherwise. To 'trade' includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of, or agreeing to apply for, acquire or dispose of, those securities, and section 7 requires prior written clearance for trading in Company Securities at any time. So writing a call and buying a put OTC over PLS shares requires prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer and is barred in a Prohibited Period absent exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over Company Securities are treated identically to OTC options; the definition of Company Securities draws no venue distinction and both are caught by the section 7 clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme. Unvested LTI/STI rights therefore cannot be collared or pledged.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of a security holding in the Company is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer. The policy does not ban hedging of vested or on-market holdings outright; it converts it into a clearance decision. Clearance is valid five business days unless the Approving Officer states otherwise.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: The policy's only division is vested versus unvested entitlements; it does not separately address shares that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or disposal restriction. Where the entitlement is still 'unvested' in substance because performance or service conditions remain, the absolute ban applies; a holding-locked but fully vested share falls under the clearance limb instead.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar limits the economic risk of the holding and so falls under section 10, and to the extent it is secured on the shares it also falls under section 11. Either way it is permitted only with prior written clearance, and any accompanying agreement to dispose is itself 'trading'.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. A short sale of Company Securities is inherently short term and speculative trading, which section 9 bans outright, and it would in any event be a disposal requiring prior written clearance under section 7.
rules.evidence: Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned, are not within the definition of 'trade' (apply for, acquire, dispose, or agree to do so), and are not caught by sections 10 or 11. A stock loan to the bank as part of a collar structure is unregulated by this policy, though the Company Secretary should be consulted.

CFDs are not named but an equity swap over Company Securities is expressly a Company Security, so acquiring one is trading requiring prior written clearance. In practice a CFD would also engage the section 9 ban on short term or speculative trading and, if short, the same objection as short selling.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loans over Company Securities are not banned; they require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer. A disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions in section 5, so a forced sale does not itself breach the policy.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company Securities is not itself listed as 'trading', but section 11 catches any secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities and requires prior written clearance. A charge or pledge unconnected with a lending arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities

rules.detail: Any secured lending in relation to Company Securities, not only margin lending, is permitted with prior written clearance. No security-state carve-out is stated for the loan itself, although section 10 separately bars limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements. The clearance decision is at the Approving Officer's discretion and no criteria are given.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: A bare, undefined prohibition on short term or speculative trading, expressed as an encouragement to adopt a long term attitude to investment. No holding period, no LIFO rule, no carve-outs and no numerical threshold are stated, so the boundary is a matter for the Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Restricted Persons to adopt a long term attitude to investment in Company Securities. Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

PLS.exemption_authority: The relevant Approving Officer (section 7) may grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period where the circumstances are exceptional (severe financial hardship, court order or other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or any other circumstance the Approving Officer deems exceptional). The same Approving Officers grant clearance for hedging, margin loans and other secured lending, and non-discretionary trading plans. There is no Board-level waiver of the absolute ban on hedging unvested entitlements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every leg of a funded collar at any time of year, not just in Blackout Periods, so entry, roll, unwind and physical settlement each need a fresh written approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lending is permitted with clearance
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a flat ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permissible here provided the Approving Officer gives prior written clearance, which makes a funded collar structurally available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs over vested shares are a clearance decision rather than a prohibition, so the whole structure turns on the Chair's or Managing Director's willingness to approve.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absolute with no clearance route, so the collar and any security must be confined to shares that have already vested and been delivered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the section 5 restrictions].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale over the collared shares in a Blackout Period does not put the executive in breach, which removes the single biggest obstacle most ASX policies present to a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of five business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced, documented and executed inside five business days unless the Approving Officer expressly extends the window in the clearance itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board from time to time ... Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed Additional Period can block execution or unwind of the collar at any time, and the executive cannot even tell the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the end of each of the March and September financial quarters and 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly reports for those financial quarters
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a mining company PLS has four closed periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undefined, so a short-dated or knock-out collar risks being characterised as speculative; a multi-year tenor with no early termination triggers is safer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are themselves Company Securities, so acquiring the put and writing the call are separately 'trading' events needing clearance and falling outside Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirement; the executive must procure compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Breach of this policy (irrespective of whether the insider trading prohibition or any other law is breached) will also be regarded by the Group as serious misconduct which may lead to disciplinary action and/or dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Executing any collar leg without written clearance is a dismissal-level offence, so the bank should condition drawdown on sighting the clearance.

PLS.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, subject to discretionary approval. Section 10 permits transactions that limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's holding, and section 11 permits margin loans and other secured lending in relation to Company Securities, in each case only with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer (the Chair for a director or KMP, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, the Managing Director for nominated Employees). The structure must be confined to vested shares, because limiting the economic risk of unvested equity scheme entitlements is prohibited absolutely with no clearance route. Execution must fall outside the four Blackout Periods (half-year, annual and the March and September quarterly reports) and any confidential Board-imposed Additional Period, must not be done while holding Inside Information, and must be completed within the five business days for which clearance is valid unless the Approving Officer states a longer period. Helpfully for the bank, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions, so enforcement over the collared shares does not breach the policy, although a short tenor or early-termination features could still fall foul of the undefined ban on short term or speculative trading.

SOL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has discretion to impose Blackout Periods, established by resolution of the Board. These are additional periods during which Directors, KMP, Employees and their Associates are prohibited from trading. The policy does not say whether their existence is confidential, but a refusal of approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on trading in any financial product issued or created over the Company's securities. There is no venue limit, no clearance route and no exception for vested or unrestricted shares, so an OTC put purchased from a bank and a call written to it are both prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: Directors, KMPs and Employees are prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company or from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Company securities are equally caught; section 11.1 makes no distinction by venue or by whether the product is issued by the Company or created by a third party.

rules.detail: Section 10.1 confines its hedging ban to unvested or holding-locked securities, so hedging of freely held shares is not caught by that limb. However section 11.1 independently prohibits trading in any financial product issued or created over the Company's securities, and every practical hedge of a vested holding (put, call, collar, swap, forward) is such a product. The result is that hedging vested unrestricted shares is prohibited by the financial products limb even though the hedging limb stops short.
rules.evidence: prohibited from ... trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid variable forward, collar-plus-loan or similar structure is a financial product created over the Company's securities and so falls within the section 11.1 prohibition; an outright sale remains available with approval.

rules.evidence: prohibited from ... trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities

SOL.exemption_authority: The Chairman (or two Directors, or one Director and the Company Secretary, and for Employees the Chairman via the CEO) may give written approval to trade during a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances, including 'other circumstances as determined by the Chairman, Directors and/or Company Secretary'. That discretion relieves only the Prohibited Period restriction; there is no stated authority to waive the section 10 hedging, short selling and short term prohibitions or the section 11 margin loan and financial products prohibition. The Board is the document approver and can amend the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, KMPs and Employees are prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company or from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: both collar legs are financial products created over Company securities, so the derivative overlay is banned outright with no approval route, regardless of vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban is narrower than the products ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: must not trade in securities of the Company ... as part of a hedging arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting their exposure to Company securities that have not vested or are subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 10 alone would permit hedging fully vested unrestricted shares, so any argument for a collar must overcome section 11.1 rather than section 10.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing ban bites only on borrowing to buy Company shares, so a bank loan secured on an existing vested holding is not expressly prohibited, leaving the derivative legs as the sole blocker.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision on granting security, charges, liens or pledges over Company securities, on forced sales by a secured lender, on margin calls, or on disclosure of encumbrances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender enforcing security during a Closed Period has no express carve-out, so the executive would have to rely on the general 'no control or influence' exclusion in section 8.1 with no certainty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This is the case even if clearance to trade securities has been granted under this policy. Such clearance is taken to be revoked if the relevant person seeking to trade is in possession of non-public price sensitive information about or affecting the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval is automatically void on receipt of inside information, so any structure must be executed immediately after approval and cannot rely on a standing consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The written approval shall have effect for a period of four weeks from the date of the approval notice or a shorter period if specified in the notice unless a material change in circumstances occurs. ... Written approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is discretionary, is not an endorsement of the proposed trade and can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the generous four-week exceptional-circumstances approval is expressly revocable, so a bank cannot treat it as a committed condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A decision to refuse approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and the executive cannot explain to the bank why a trade date was missed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to trading in the securities of Washington H. Soul Pattinson and Company Limited, those of its controlled and associated entities and those of entities in which it has a Substantial Interest [5% or more of the voting shares].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over shares in any listed investee in which SOL holds 5% or more also needs Chairman approval, which matters given SOL's investment portfolio.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 10.1 and 11.1 bind 'Directors, KMPs and Employees' whereas sections 2.2, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1 and 9.1 bind those persons 'and their Associates'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The drafting arguably leaves Associates outside the financial products ban, but the Associate definition and the approval requirement make any attempt to structure around it plainly against the policy's intent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A breach of this policy will be recorded, and serious breaches will be reported to the Leadership Team and the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering a collar without approval would be escalated to the Board rather than handled informally, with termination of employment expressly contemplated.

SOL.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 11.1 prohibits Directors, KMP and Employees from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities, which captures both the purchased put and the written call whether traded OTC or on exchange, with no clearance route, no exceptional-circumstances relief and no distinction by vesting state. The section 10.1 hedging ban is narrower, reaching only arrangements that limit exposure to unvested or holding-locked securities, and the margin loan ban in section 11.1 is narrower still, reaching only borrowing used to finance the purchase of Company shares, so the secured loan leg over an existing vested holding is not itself expressly prohibited. That is of no assistance while the derivative overlay remains banned, and the policy is silent on encumbrances, margin calls and forced sales, giving a lender no comfort that enforcement during a Closed Period would be excused. In practice an executive can only sell outright, with prior Chairman approval, outside the 1 January and 1 July Closed Periods and any Board-imposed Blackout Period.
