bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates are prohibited from ... entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition on granting security is deliberately confined to vested-but-restricted securities, so a security interest over freely held vested securities is not prohibited, which is what makes a funded collar arguable at Vicinity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, which may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of VCX securities, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Properly described as margin lending arrangements' is narrower than a general secured financing ban, so a bilateral term loan with a fixed advance and no maintenance margin is arguably outside it, but the facility must be structured and documented so it is not in substance a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: VCX securities: Any Securities of Vicinity Centres and any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call written by the bank are themselves VCX securities, so entry, roll, unwind and settlement each require the dual approvals and must fall outside a blackout period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban tied to remuneration status
bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar may only be written over securities that have vested and are free of any trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so the bank must diligence clawback and holding-lock terms in the plan documents, not just vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The section 7 exclusions from the blackout restrictions cover only plan option exercises, takeover acceptances and transfers out of the employee share plan trust with no change in beneficial ownership.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike Ramsay or MinRes, Vicinity has no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so enforcement or physical settlement during a blackout period would be an unexcused dealing and a Policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The test compares any two dealings in any VCX securities, and derivatives count, so the option legs and any share dealing must be spaced at least 30 days apart and settlement must not follow a recent acquisition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Chairman – approval from both the Chairman of the Audit Committee and the CEO; Other Directors – both the Chairman of the Board and the CEO; CEO – both the Chairman of the Board and the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or Group Company Secretary; All other Restricted Officers – any two of the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or the Group Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Two approvers are required for every leg, which lengthens lead time and means the structure must be explained to Board-level approvers before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A written response to a trading request should be given within two business days of the initial request. Trading by a Restricted Officer may be conducted no more than five business days after the trading request has been approved. ... Any trading request can be approved or not approved without giving reasons and can be withdrawn by email if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, and approval can be withdrawn by email at any point before the trade, which the bank must accommodate as a condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A decision not to approve a trading request is final and binding on the individual seeking approval. A refusal to approve a trading request is confidential information and must not be disclosed to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a leg has been blocked, so the documents should not require the client to explain a refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the intention of this Policy not only to minimise the risk of insider trading but also to avoid the appearance of insider trading and the significant reputational damage that may cause
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval turns partly on appearances, so a collar over a large proportion of a director's holding is likely to be refused even where technically permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Officer, their spouse or partner or their dependent children, are or may be a beneficiary; and any company in which the Restricted Officer, or any of the above-mentioned persons, directly or indirectly holds a majority of the shares or otherwise controls or significantly influences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'may be a beneficiary' and 'significantly influences' limbs are wide, so almost any family holding vehicle used as borrower or collar counterparty is itself bound by the section 8 prohibitions and the approval regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Vicinity, Vicinity Centres or the Group means the stapled group of Vicinity Limited and Vicinity Centres Trust, of which Vicinity Centres RE Ltd is the responsible entity; 'securities' includes any unit or other interest in the scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The underlying is a stapled security comprising a share and a trust unit, so the collar confirmations and the security documents must describe the stapled security correctly and deal with a possible destapling.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy also applies to employees on extended leave from Vicinity, including parental leave, personal leave, long service leave, a career break or leave without pay.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Time away from the business does not suspend the approval requirements or the section 8 prohibitions for the life of the collar.

VCX.summary: A funded collar is arguable at Vicinity but only over securities that have vested and are free of any trading restriction or forfeiture condition, and it requires careful structuring of the loan. Section 8 imposes three absolute, approval-proof bans on Restricted Officers and their Close Associates: hedging anything that is unvested, restricted or forfeitable; granting a security interest over vested securities that remain restricted or forfeitable; and entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements. Neither the security interest ban nor the margin lending ban reaches a bilateral term loan secured on freely held vested securities, so the funded leg is available if the facility is genuinely not a margin loan, has no maintenance margin, and is documented as such. The option legs are themselves VCX securities because the definition captures derivatives entered into with a third party, so entry, roll and unwind each need two named approvers (Chairman of the Board and CEO for a director), a written response within two business days, execution within five, notification to the Company Secretary within two business days of the trade and, for directors, an ASX report, all outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any email-notified extension. Two risks stand out: there is no exclusion for a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights, so enforcement or physical settlement in a blackout would breach the Policy, and the 30-day short-term dealing test compares any two dealings in any VCX securities, derivatives included.

tiers.name: Company Personnel

The Board may only add further Approved Trading Periods ('any other period as determined by the Board from time to time'), and the Managing Director may determine additional officers or persons to whom the policy applies, which can bring a person within the Approved Trading Period regime.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no venue limit and no approval route, on any use of Derivatives over unvested Equity Interests by Company Personnel holding them and by their Connected Persons. Derivatives is defined to include put and call options and 'caps and collars', so a collar over unvested shares, options or performance rights is squarely caught.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel may use Derivatives, including OTC puts, calls and collars, over vested Company Securities subject only to the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the balance of the policy. No notice or approval is required of them.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Securities are expressly allowed, but for Designated Personnel entry into the derivative is Trading that must occur inside an Approved Trading Period and requires prior approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, plus written confirmation to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Personnel of the Company must seek approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade.

rules.detail: A director may enter a Derivative over vested Securities in an Approved Trading Period after informing the Chair (the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee); no approval is required, only prior notice, followed by written advice to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for ASX notification within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: A director of the Company must inform the Chair prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade;

rules.detail: The rationale given is that hedging unvested equity would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met and would break the connection between staff performance and shareholder interests. 'Any other hedging or investment arrangement' falls within the defined term Derivatives, so the ban is not limited to listed instruments.
rules.evidence: The use of Derivatives over unvested Company's Securities may allow value to be realised from those Securities even if performance hurdles have not been met. This would break the intended connection between staff performance and shareholder best interests.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities is expressly permitted rather than merely unaddressed, because 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' is a Derivative and section 7 permits Derivatives over vested Securities. Subject to Approved Trading Periods, prior approval or notice, the speculative trading ban and the 'front page' test.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, structured financial product or collar is within the definition of Derivatives and its entry is Trading (an agreement to sell or grant an option), so it is permitted over vested Securities but only in an Approved Trading Period with prior approval. Note that a short-dated forward risks being caught by the speculative trading ban, which names forward contracts as short term Trading.
rules.evidence: Trading means taking part in any transaction associated with applying for, buying, acquiring, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting, assigning rights to buy, sell or subscribe for, or agreeing to do any of these things

rules.detail: Any monetisation of unvested Equity Interests would be effected through a Derivative (forward, structured financial product, collar or 'any other hedging or investment arrangement') and is therefore banned outright.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Outright ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons. The policy defines short selling narrowly as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back lower, so a covered collar over shares actually held is not short selling on the policy's own definition.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Section 10 is directed only at Designated Personnel; Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel are not covered by an express short selling ban.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the definition of Trading. Borrowing securities is mentioned only descriptively in explaining what short selling is.

Contracts for difference and spread bets are expressly named as Derivatives. They are permitted in principle over vested Securities under section 7, but in practice a CFD over Company Securities is short term Trading caught by the speculative trading ban and, if short, by the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in speculative Trading in the Company's securities, such as Trading on considerations of a short term nature.

rules.detail: Flat ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons entering margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company Securities, with no vesting-state qualification, no approval route and no exemption. The phrase 'any margin lending arrangements' is broad enough to capture a bank loan margined against, and secured on, the collared shares.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons; the policy says nothing about margin lending by other Company Personnel.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not mentioned, and the definition of Trading covers buying, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting and assigning rights but not the creation of a security interest. There is no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.

The only financing prohibition is section 8, confined to 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements'. There is no general ban on secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, and no rule on what happens if a lender forces a sale. Whether a funded collar loan is caught turns on whether it is characterised as a margin lending arrangement.

Speculative Trading is banned, defined to include buying and selling Securities within a six month period and entering into other short term Trading, with forward contracts given as the example. Sale of shares received on vesting of employee incentives is carved out. This makes instrument tenor material: a collar maturing inside six months, or one written as a short-dated forward, is exposed to this prohibition.
rules.evidence: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).

rules.detail: Section 9 applies only to Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons.

ALQ.exemption_authority: Chair, at complete discretion, may grant prior written clearance to sell outside an Approved Trading Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or overriding legal requirement, or a pressing financial commitment); if the Chair is the applicant, the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee decides. The clearance is valid for seven business days, can be withdrawn on a change of circumstances, lapses immediately on acquiring Inside Information, and clears a breach of the policy only, not the insider trading laws. It extends to selling only, not to entering derivatives or financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are expressly within the defined term with no venue limit, so section 7 governs the structure directly: banned over unvested securities, permitted over vested ones.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a rare affirmative permission for hedging vested shares, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are contemplated rather than merely unprohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to margin loans strictly so called; a bank facility secured on the collared shares with margin or top-up mechanics is likely an 'arrangement in respect of Company's Securities' and would need to be structured, and confirmed with the Company Secretary, to sit outside it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no prohibition on pledging, charging or otherwise encumbering Company Securities other than section 8 on margin loans, and no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A non-margin term loan secured on the collared shares is not caught by any express prohibition, which is the key point of difference from policies that ban all secured financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar tenor should comfortably exceed six months and should not be documented as a forward, or it risks being characterised as speculative short term Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel ... are prohibited from Trading ... outside of the following periods: a period of one month commencing on the business day after the day full year results are announced; ... half year results ...; ... the Company's annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and any physical settlement of the collar must each fall inside one of only three one-month windows a year, and there is no exceptional-circumstances relief for anything other than a sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is silent on sales effected by a third party such as a lender, on margin calls and on price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither excused nor declared a breach: lender enforcement or cash-settlement outside a window is unregulated by the text but would sit uneasily with the window regime, so the facility should avoid discretionary lender sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances surrounding the Company, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Company Personnel or their Connected Persons taking advantage of their position in an inappropriate way? ... Any Trade in Company Securities ... must not be made if that Trade would fail the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-textured veto that sits above the express permissions, so the Chair or Managing Director can decline a collar on reputational grounds even where every specific rule is satisfied.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also applies to the Connected Persons of the Company Personnel ... or a company, trust or entity that the person or any of their Connected Persons controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the margin lending ban, the trading windows or the notice requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It is recognised that in exceptional circumstances, a Designated Personnel or their Connected Persons may need to sell the Company's Securities outside of an Approved Trading Period. ... A clearance is valid for seven business days from the date of the notification and can be withdrawn if there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only out-of-window relief is for a sale, so an urgent collar unwind or restructure outside a window has no sanctioned route.

ALQ.summary: A funded collar is possible for an ALS director or executive over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating on the derivative legs. Section 7 expressly permits the use of Derivatives, a term that names 'caps and collars' and 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' without venue limitation, in relation to vested Company Securities, while banning them outright over unvested equity incentives. The constraints are procedural and timing-based: Designated Personnel may only Trade in one of three one-month Approved Trading Periods following full year results, half year results and the AGM, a director must first inform the Chair and other Designated Personnel must obtain approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, written confirmation goes to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, and the tenor must exceed six months to avoid the speculative trading ban on buying and selling within six months and on forward contracts. The loan leg is the live issue: there is no general prohibition on secured financing or on encumbering shares, but section 8 bans Designated Personnel from 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities', so the facility must be a fixed term loan without margin or top-up mechanics and should be confirmed in advance with the Company Secretary. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or lender enforcement, so any lender sale right should be exercisable only within an Approved Trading Period, and the Chair's exceptional-circumstances discretion covers sales only and would not authorise an out-of-window unwind.

rules.section: Key Principles; Margin lending and other security interests
rules.detail: The second limb of the margin lending clause is a general ban on secured financing: no rights of any kind may be granted to a lender over the person's Lottery Corporation Securities. This is the decisive obstacle to the loan leg of a funded collar and there is no discretion to waive it, the exceptional circumstances relief being limited to selling or disposing of Securities.

TLC.exemption_authority: MD & CEO, or the Chairman in the case of Directors, may grant pre-clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Blackout Period or on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a pressing financial commitment, court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement) where the Trading is the only reasonable course of action available. The relief runs to sales and disposals only; there is no power to waive the hedging, margin lending or security interest prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: grant of any rights to lenders
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any The Lottery Corporation Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The second limb is a flat ban on giving a financier any rights over the shares, which defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar regardless of vesting state, loan purpose or loan-to-value ratio.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees, Directors and their Associates are prohibited from engaging in Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending, and from granting any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Key Principles restate the ban without even the word 'lenders', so on the policy's own summary a written call option granted over the shares to the bank is at risk of being read as a prohibited grant of rights, not merely the security interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Security Trading covered by this Policy includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every element of a funded collar, the put, the call, the charge and the loan, is separately a Trade requiring written pre-clearance and falling outside Blackout Periods, so there is no argument that only the share sale is regulated.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restricted shares included in hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights; and entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only shares that are both vested and free of plan restrictions can be collared, so the collar pool must be carefully identified against the plan records.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Trading that is the subject of pre-clearance must be executed within three business days of the receipt of the written pre-clearance (unless the pre-clearance is withdrawn).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The whole structure would have to be priced, documented and executed inside three business days of clearance, and the clearance can be withdrawn in the meantime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any pre-clearance to Trade can be given, withdrawn, refused or made subject to conditions by the applicable approver in their absolute discretion and without giving reasons. If pre-clearance is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the pre-clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on obtaining or keeping clearance, and the executive may be barred from explaining to the bank why a trade cannot proceed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An application for pre-clearance to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the derivative legs can be refused if the collar would leave the director or executive short of the minimum shareholding, so the collared parcel should sit above that requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Continuous Disclosure Committee may also, from time to time without prior notice, and conditionally or unconditionally, extend, reduce, or create an additional Blackout Period. ... The Board or Chairman may also, from time to time, at their absolute discretion, and without prior notice, impose ad hoc restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the executive bears that timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term Trading (Trading within six months of the acquisition) of The Lottery Corporation Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind must sit beyond six months from the acquisition of the underlying shares, or fall within the narrow exceptional circumstances relief.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates means any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with The Lottery Corporation or any of its Directors or Team Members (such as spouses, partners, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, joint venture partners).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family trust, family company or self-managed superannuation fund does not escape the security interest ban or the pre-clearance regime.

TLC.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a Lottery Corporation Director or Restricted Employee. The derivative legs alone would be workable over vested, unrestricted shares: the hedging and derivatives ban is confined to restricted shares and unvested performance options and rights, Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps and hedges whether cash settled or not, and creating a hedge is simply Trading that requires written pre-clearance from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (Restricted Employees), executed within three business days, outside the 1 January, 1 July and 1 October Blackout Periods and any additional blackout imposed by the Continuous Disclosure Committee. The loan leg fails: Directors and Restricted Employees and their Associates must not 'grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities', an unqualified prohibition with no vesting-state limit, no threshold and no waiver power, and the Key Principles state it even more broadly as a ban on 'granting any rights over' their Securities. The exceptional circumstances discretion extends only to selling or disposing of Securities in hardship or under legal compulsion, so it cannot be used to authorise a secured facility. Any structure would therefore have to be unsecured and cash settled, sit beyond six months from acquisition to avoid the Short-term Trading ban, and leave the executive compliant with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy, since pre-clearance may be refused on that ground.

ASX.title: ASX Group Dealing Rules Policy (Version 8.0)

tiers.name: ASX People
tiers.description: All ASX people including fixed-term staff, direct contractors, casuals, secondees, consultants deemed subject to the Policy by People and Culture, and ASX Group directors. Must pre-clear all dealing in Covered Securities, may deal in ASX Group Securities only in a designated ASX Trading Window, must deal within five business days of clearance, and are subject to the three-month short-term dealing ban, the hedging ban over unvested and holding-locked securities and the collateral ban.

tiers.name: ASX Group Executives
tiers.description: ASX Group Executives. Distinguished only by the obligation to notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities, which may be publicly disclosed.

tiers.name: ASX Group Directors
tiers.description: ASX Group directors. Subject to the whole Policy as ASX People, plus the notification to the Company Secretary of any derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. Pre-clearance for ASX Limited NEDs comes from the Chair of ASX Limited (alternate: Group General Counsel or Chief Risk Officer); the Chair of ASX Limited is cleared by the Chair of the Board Risk Committee.

tiers.name: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors of ASX Limited and of the CS facility licensees. The Policy's restrictions apply to them only in relation to ASX Group Securities and no pre-clearance is needed for non-ASX Group Securities. All their dealings in ASX Group Securities must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days whether or not the beneficial holding changes, and short-term dealing within three months is prohibited.

tiers.name: NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors on the boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees. Prohibited from holding ASX Group securities at all; those holding on appointment must divest promptly and in compliance with the Policy.

tiers.name: Chief Compliance Officer and people in Listings Compliance, the Market Announcements Office and Surveillance
tiers.description: Must not hold, deal in or have an interest in Covered Securities, except securities held before appointment (which may be held but not dealt), corporate actions on pre-held securities, acceptance of a takeover or scheme, participation in ASX Employee Share Plans, and dealing in ASX Group securities in a designated Trading Window with pre-clearance.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: An ASX person's spouse, de facto partner, children residing with them, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds or other entities controlled by the ASX person and/or their Connected Persons. ASX People must take reasonable steps to inform them of the Policy and ensure they comply with it as if they were the ASX person.

rules.section: 2.5 (Derivatives and hedging arrangements over ASX Group Securities)
rules.detail: Absolute ban on any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities, with no venue limit and no approval route. A collar is squarely a transaction that limits economic risk.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The ban expressly extends to vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock, so the collar pool must be limited to vested shares free of any holding lock.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked ASX Group Securities is expressly contemplated rather than prohibited. The only stated requirement for directors is notification to the Company Secretary, and the position may be publicly disclosed. Pre-clearance under section 2.2 is expressed to apply to dealing in Covered Securities, which are financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, so an over-the-counter hedge is not itself a Covered Security, but the Policy requires compliance with its spirit as well as its letter.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.

rules.detail: Same position as directors: permitted over vested unlocked securities, subject to notifying the Company Secretary and possible public disclosure. No deadline or form is specified for the notification.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: A put, call or collar over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities limits economic risk and is caught by the express prohibition, whatever the venue.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and derivatives quoted on an Australian financial market are Covered Securities, so dealing in them requires pre-clearance through the online form, must be executed within five business days, and, where they are over ASX Group Securities, only in a designated ASX Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, debentures and hybrids, warrants, futures, options, derivatives and single-entity Exchange Traded Products (ETPs) ... You must not deal in Covered Securities without ASX pre-clearance approval.

rules.detail: An over-the-counter put or call is not quoted on an Australian financial market and so is not a Covered Security or a Security as defined, meaning the pre-clearance machinery does not by its terms bite on the derivative itself. What the Policy does require is notification to the Company Secretary of a derivative position over vested ASX Group Securities.
rules.evidence: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market.

rules.tier: NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees
rules.detail: These directors may not hold ASX Group securities at all and must divest any held on appointment, so there is no shareholding over which a collar could be written.
rules.evidence: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited (with any directors who hold ASX Group Securities prior to their appointment being required to divest those shares promptly and compliantly with this Policy).

rules.section: 2.5 (ASX Group Securities margin loans and other financing arrangements)
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Any monetisation that advances cash against the shares is a financing arrangement, and using ASX Group Securities as collateral for it is prohibited outright. An unsecured cash-settled monetisation would instead be treated as a hedging or derivative position requiring notification by executives and directors.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the three-month purchase-then-sale prohibition and by the requirement to pre-clear dealing in Covered Securities.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of Deal, which is confined to buying, acquiring, selling, transferring, disposing or converting Covered Securities or agreeing to do so.

Contracts for difference are not named. They are not quoted on an Australian financial market and so are not Covered Securities, but a CFD over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities would be caught by the ban on transactions limiting economic risk.

Flat ban on using ASX Group Securities as collateral for a new margin loan, with an added obligation to ensure that any portfolio of Covered Securities given as collateral contains no ASX Group Securities. Margin loans and financing over non-ASX Group Securities do not even require pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: Pledging or charging ASX Group Securities to any financier is prohibited because it is the use of those securities as collateral. The prohibition is framed by reference to entering a new margin loan or financing arrangement, so an encumbrance unconnected with financing is not expressly addressed, and creating a security interest is not itself within the definition of Deal.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans; it reaches any 'other financing arrangement' collateralised by ASX Group Securities, applies to all ASX people and their Connected Persons and to all vesting states, and applies to new arrangements. There is no approval route, although the section 2.8 waiver power is expressed to cover the Policy's dealing prohibitions generally.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: No purchase then sale, or sale then purchase, of Covered Securities of the same entity within three months. Market volatility is expressly rejected as a ground for exemption, and dealing that ASX considers frequent may also be denied clearance.

ASX.exemption_authority: Waivers from the Policy's dealing prohibitions may be granted in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, a transfer under a family law property settlement, a testamentary disposition) where the proposed dealing is the only reasonable course of action available and the applicant holds no Inside Information; waivers may be conditional. Granted by the General Manager, Enterprise Risk and Compliance (alternate Chief Risk Officer or Group General Counsel) for ASX people and Connected Persons; by the CEO or Group General Counsel for the Chief Compliance Officer; by the Chair of ASX Limited (having consulted the Group General Counsel or Company Secretary) for the CEO; and by the Chair of ASX Limited for ASX Limited and subsidiary NEDs. Requests go to enterprise.compliance@asx.com.au.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar outright, including the technique of pledging a diversified portfolio that happens to contain ASX shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financing terms must not allow out-of-window sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the terms of your margin loan or financing arrangement does not require, nor allow for, ASX Group Securities to be disposed of at such time that would breach this Policy, such as outside of a designated ASX Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a lawful financing arrangement must be documented so that the lender has no right to sell ASX shares outside a Trading Window, which rules out ordinary bank enforcement and margin-call mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging vested shares is permitted but disclosable
bespoke_clauses.clause: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares is permitted, but the executive must accept notification and possible public disclosure of the position.

bespoke_clauses.topic: holding lock extends the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough; any holding lock on the shares must have lifted before they can be included in the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC instruments fall outside Covered Securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market. Covered Securities: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, options, derivatives, warrants, futures debentures, hybrids and single-entity ETPs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An over-the-counter put or call is not a Covered Security, so the pre-clearance and Trading Window machinery does not by its terms apply to the derivative legs, only the express hedging rule and the notification obligation do, but the 'letter and spirit' clause makes it prudent to pre-clear anyway.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may request a waiver from this Policy's dealing prohibitions in certain exceptional circumstances, including: severe financial hardship ... The proposed dealing is to be the only reasonable course of action available to you and any granted waiver may be subject to conditions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a secured facility, but it is limited to exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, so it cannot support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The ASX Board may decline to open a Trading Window during the periods listed above. The ASX Board may also elect to shorten, change or close a ASX Trading Window at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no guaranteed window, so any collar entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, including, but not limited, to: ... matters known to ASX, but not to you, and your ASX authorisation officer determines pre-clearance should not be granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the executive being able to trade at any particular time, and no reason for a refusal need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy contains a set of principles. You must comply with both the letter and spirit of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A structure engineered around the definition of Covered Securities to escape pre-clearance is exposed to challenge on spirit grounds even if the literal wording permits it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: CS licensee directors cannot hold at all
bespoke_clauses.clause: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For that group there is no underlying shareholding at all, so no collar, funded or otherwise, is possible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Persons are ASX peoples' spouse, de facto partner, children residing with the ASX person, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) or other entities controlled by an ASX person and/or their Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares in a family trust, company or SMSF does not avoid the collateral ban or the pre-clearance and window regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must deal within five business days once ASX pre-clearance approval has been granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared leg must be executed within five business days, which is workable for a negotiated OTC trade but leaves no room for extended documentation.

ASX.summary: A funded collar is not possible for an ASX Limited director or executive, although the derivative legs alone are. Section 2.5 expressly permits transactions limiting economic risk over vested ASX Group Securities that are not subject to a holding lock, banning them only over unvested or holding-locked securities, and the only formality for ASX Group Executives and Directors is notification to the Company Secretary, with possible public disclosure; the OTC legs are not themselves Covered Securities, though the Policy's 'letter and spirit' clause makes pre-clearance prudent and any exchange-traded leg would require it, be executable only within five business days and confined to a Trading Window opened at the ASX Board's discretion after half-year results, full-year results and the AGM. The loan leg fails outright: ASX people are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement, and must ensure that any collateral portfolio contains no ASX Group Securities. The Policy goes further and requires that the terms of any financing arrangement neither require nor allow ASX Group Securities to be disposed of outside a Trading Window, which would rule out conventional lender enforcement and margin-call rights even if collateral were permitted. The only conceivable route is a section 2.8 waiver from Enterprise Risk and Compliance or the Chair for severe financial hardship where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, which will not support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar, and Non-Executive Directors of the Clearing & Settlement facility licensees may not hold ASX Group securities at all.

rules.detail: Absolute, permanent ban on dealing in Derivatives over Securities by every Employee, including non-executive Directors, the Managing Director and Senior Executives, and their Associates. There is no vesting-state qualification, no venue limit, no consent route and no exemption; the Exceptional Circumstances relief in section 5.1 is confined to selling or disposing of Securities.
rules.evidence: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.

rules.detail: The defined term Derivatives is an effects-based hedging definition: any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities, now or in the future. Both legs of a collar and the collar as a whole fall within it, so hedging of vested, unrestricted Stockland securities is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but any prepaid forward, structured product or similar is a 'like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities' and is banned by section 5.3(a), and any monetisation that gives the financier recourse to the Securities is banned by the Security Interest prohibition in section 5.3(b).
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Flat ban on short selling Securities by all Employees. The term is not defined, so the ordinary meaning applies.
rules.evidence: Employees must not short-sell Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. Deal is defined only as directly or indirectly acquiring or disposing of Securities. A stock loan to a financier would in any event be caught by the ban on giving 'security or other right to a lender or financier' over Securities.

Contracts for difference are not named but are a derivative or like instrument limiting exposure to the market price of Securities, so they fall inside the defined term Derivatives and within the absolute ban. A short CFD would separately breach the short selling prohibition.
rules.evidence: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.

rules.detail: All Employees, including non-executive Directors, and their Associates are banned from entering any margin lending arrangement. Only Security Interests existing before the Policy was approved are grandfathered.
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Creating or giving a mortgage, security or any other right to a lender or financier over any Securities is prohibited. The definition of Security Interest is deliberately wide, reaching not only formal security but 'other right' given to a lender or financier. Pre-existing Security Interests are excluded from the Policy's operation.
rules.evidence: create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities. Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not confined to margin loans; it captures any arrangement under which a lender or financier is given a mortgage, security or other right over Stockland Securities, whatever the loan-to-value ratio or purpose. There is no approval route and no waiver power for it.
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Consent will generally not be given for short-term trading, defined as buying and selling Securities within a six month period. Expressed as a consent policy rather than an absolute ban, but for Employees who need no consent in a Permitted Trading Window it operates as a statement of expectation that they be long-term investors.
rules.evidence: Consent under section 5.1 will generally not be given to allow an Employee to engage in short-term trading of Securities. An Employee would be engaging in short-term trading of Securities if they were to buy and sell Securities within a six (6) month period.

The Managing Director and Senior Executives may not dispose of Securities acquired from awards under Stockland equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010 unless immediately after the disposal they would still hold Securities worth two times Fixed Pay (Managing Director) or one times Fixed Pay (other Senior Executives), with a carve-out for sales reasonably necessary to pay tax on vesting under a long term incentive plan. SGP.exemption_authority: The Consent Authority may consent to Dealing in a Prohibited Period only where Exceptional Circumstances exist (severe financial hardship with a pressing financial commitment, a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement, or other exceptional circumstances where sale is the only reasonable course of action). The relief is expressed in terms of selling Securities and does not extend to the section 5.3 prohibitions on Derivatives and Security Interests, which have no waiver mechanism. Consent will not be given if there is any possibility that the Policy could be breached, no reasons are given, the decision is final and binding, and a refusal must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of the collar are prohibited for everyone the Policy covers, at every vesting state, with no consent route and no waiver, so the structure fails before the financing is even considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition turns on economic effect rather than instrument type, so a cash-settled, synthetic or forward-starting structure is caught just as squarely as a physically settled put and call.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is separately prohibited, and the words 'or other right to a lender or financier' are wide enough to catch even a negative pledge or a call option written in favour of the financing bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only permitted encumbrances are those predating the Policy's approval in May 2025, so no new facility can be granted and the exclusion cannot be extended to a refinancing or an increase.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptional Circumstances means where: (a) the Director, Senior Executive or Employee is suffering severe financial hardship ... (c) there are other exceptional circumstances for which the sale of the Securities is the only reasonable course of action available.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every limb of the exceptional circumstances relief is framed around selling Securities, so there is no route to a hedged or financed position even in hardship; the only sanctioned answer to a liquidity need is an outright sale with consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: settlement must complete inside the window
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Deal or Dealing in Securities will be within a Permitted Trading Window if the trade has been settled and completed before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window. ... If the transaction has not been completed or settled before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window at 4pm (AEST) on that day ... the Employee must cancel the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually strict: settlement, not execution, must fall inside the window, so any physically settled leg would need to complete well before the window closes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: These executives are prohibited from disposing of Securities acquired from awards under any Stockland equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010, unless immediately after that disposal they would continue to hold a minimum number of Securities with a value being the equivalent of two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times Fixed Pay for all other Senior Executives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an outright sale, the only permitted form of monetisation, is floored at two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times for other Senior Executives.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent will not be given under section 5.1 if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached. No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities. The decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the person seeking consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'any possibility' standard means a Consent Authority could not approve any transaction with a bank that touches the derivative or security interest prohibitions, and there is no appeal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairperson may, at any time, through written notification to Employees impose an additional period for which Employees (or a specific group) are prohibited from Dealing in Securities while Stockland is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. This additional period may be temporary or permanent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A blackout can be imposed indefinitely and must be kept confidential, so even a permitted sale can become impossible without the executive being able to explain why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means persons and entities closely connected to a Director or Employee and includes a spouse, domestic partner, child or dependent ... company controlled by the Director or Employee and any other closely related party, as defined in the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a spouse, family company or other closely related party does not avoid either prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: the Director or Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; the trading plan does not permit the Director or Employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to undertake Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only sanctioned way to obtain scheduled liquidity outside a window is a cleared non-discretionary sale plan, which is the realistic alternative to offer in place of a collar.

SGP.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Stockland director or executive, and this is one of the clearest prohibitions in the market. Section 5.3(a) states that Employees, a term that expressly includes non-executive Directors as well as the Managing Director and Senior Executives, must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time, and Derivatives is defined by economic effect as any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities, now or in the future, so both collar legs are banned regardless of vesting state, venue or settlement method. Section 5.3(b) independently bans any margin lending arrangement and the creation or giving of a mortgage, security or other right to a lender or financier over any Securities, with only Security Interests existing before the Policy's approval grandfathered, so the secured loan leg fails as well. There is no consent route to either prohibition: the Exceptional Circumstances relief is drafted entirely around selling Securities, consent will not be given if there is any possibility the Policy could be breached, and a refusal is final, confidential and unreasoned. The only sanctioned liquidity routes are an outright sale in a six-week Permitted Trading Window, settled before the window closes and subject to the two times and one times Fixed Pay holding floors, or a pre-cleared non-discretionary trading plan.

rules.detail: The express permission to hedge vested and unrestricted securities is withdrawn from Designated Personnel, who are banned from hedging activity in any circumstances. Since Designated Personnel captures every Director of a Group Company, the Executive Leadership Team, restricted list members and their controlled entities and family, this removes the collar for exactly the population a bank would target.
rules.evidence: This permission does not apply to Designated Personnel. Designated Personnel are prohibited from hedging activity in any circumstances.

rules.detail: Personnel who are not Designated Personnel may hedge vested and unrestricted Sandfire securities, but the hedge is itself a dealing, so it cannot be entered, renewed, altered or closed out in a Blackout Period or while the person holds market sensitive information, and the short-term dealing and short selling restrictions still apply.
rules.evidence: Personnel are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Sandfire securities provided the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Sandfire securities for the purposes of this Policy.

rules.detail: Participants in an employee, executive or director equity plan must not hedge securities allocated under the plan while they remain subject to the plan rules.
rules.evidence: Personnel who participate in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Sandfire must not enter any hedging arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Sandfire securities allocated under such plan while those securities remain subject to the rules of that plan or are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The plan hedging ban runs until the securities are both free of the plan rules and free of any holding lock, so vesting alone does not release them into the hedgeable pool.
rules.evidence: while those securities remain subject to the rules of that plan or are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: A purchased put and written call over Sandfire securities are transactions in financial products using derivatives that operate to limit the economic risk of holding those securities, so they fall within the defined term Hedging and within the absolute prohibition on Designated Personnel hedging activity. There is no venue limitation.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering transactions in financial products (using derivatives or otherwise) that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Sandfire securities.

rules.detail: Non-designated Personnel may use derivatives to hedge vested and unrestricted securities, but must avoid instruments that are short term or speculative or that otherwise enable them to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities, and must transact outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: Personnel are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Sandfire securities provided the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Sandfire securities for the purposes of this Policy.

rules.detail: Exchange traded options, share warrants and similar instruments are named as examples of prohibited short-term dealings where they are short term or speculative, subject only to an Approver's approval in an exceptional circumstance.

Approval is sought from the Company Secretary, with confirmation of no market sensitive information; for Designated Personnel the Company Secretary must also obtain the Approver's approval, and the Remuneration Committee's in certain circumstances. What is exceptional is assessed case by case in the absolute discretion of the Company Secretary and Approver and may include severe financial hardship or compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertaking. bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedging ban on Designated Personnel
bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Sandfire securities provided the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Sandfire securities for the purposes of this Policy. This permission does not apply to Designated Personnel. Designated Personnel are prohibited from hedging activity in any circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: every Director, the Executive Leadership Team, restricted list members and their controlled entities and family are banned from the derivative legs outright, so no collar can be offered to them even though the financing side would be workable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: security ban limited to unvested and locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Sandfire securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock to secure any obligation of that relevant Personnel or any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, the encumbrance ban stops at unvested and holding-locked securities, so a charge over vested unrestricted shares is not prohibited and the loan leg of a funded structure is available in principle.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notwithstanding the procedures set out in this Policy, Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities in the Company where the disposal is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Rare and valuable: lender enforcement is carved out of the Blackout Period and approval machinery altogether, subject only to notifying the Company Secretary within two business days, so a bank's security can be enforced without putting the borrower in breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any dealing in Sandfire securities by Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is prohibited. This includes: entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of Sandfire's securities; transferring securities in Sandfire into an existing margin loan account; and selling Sandfire securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The facility must be a fixed term loan without margin call or top-up mechanics, and the shares must not be moved into a margin account, or the arrangement is caught notwithstanding the narrow security-granting ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes ... entering other short-term dealings (for example, transactions in derivative markets involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative) or otherwise enable Personnel to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A purchased put pays out as the price falls, so even for non-designated Personnel the collar should be structured and documented as protection of a held position over a tenor beyond three months, not as a speculative instrument.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances can lift any prohibition
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances, and only with prior approval, Personnel may deal in Sandfire securities during a Blackout Period, or in another way otherwise prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route for a Designated Person, since it purports to reach any prohibition, but it sits in tension with the statement that Designated Personnel are prohibited from hedging 'in any circumstances' and requires the Company Secretary, the Approver and sometimes the Remuneration Committee to agree.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March or 30 September each year until the commencement of trading on the ASX on the day following the day on which the relevant quarterly report for those financial quarters is released to the ASX
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly blackouts on top of the half and full year blackouts leave four closed periods a year, so entry, roll and unwind timing is materially constrained for a company on a quarterly reporting cycle.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to deal is granted, the Designated Personnel must undertake the intended dealing within two business days or such longer period that is advised by the approver (which may not be longer than five business days) following the day clearance is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved leg must be executed within two business days, extendable to five at the Approver's discretion, and the approval may be revoked at any time before then.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An application for approval to deal in Sandfire securities may be refused where the relevant person is not, or as a result of the proposed dealing will not be, in compliance with the Guideline (including the Share Selling Principles).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretariat Function screens for Guideline compliance before the request even reaches the Approver, so a structure that reduces effective exposure may be refused on that ground.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would be perceived that Personnel might be taking advantage of their position or could possibly be damaging to Sandfire's reputation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-textured veto sitting above the specific rules, which a hedging or financing structure involving a bank would have to survive.

bespoke_clauses.topic: controlled entities and family are Designated Personnel
bespoke_clauses.clause: as it relates to the persons referred to above: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to above; and a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child (including a step-child or adopted child), a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban follows the shares into family trusts, controlled companies and family members' hands, so the structure cannot be moved to an associate to escape it.

SFR.summary: A funded collar is not available to a Sandfire director or executive, but the obstacle is the derivative legs rather than the financing. Sandfire expressly permits Personnel to hedge vested and unrestricted securities, treating the hedge as a dealing, but immediately withdraws that permission from Designated Personnel, who are 'prohibited from hedging activity in any circumstances', and Designated Personnel captures every Director of a Group Company, the Executive Leadership Team, restricted list members and their controlled companies, trusts and close family. The financing side is unusually accommodating: the ban on granting security is confined to securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock, so a charge over vested unrestricted shares is not prohibited, and the Exceptions list expressly permits a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights at any time, subject only to notifying the Company Secretary within two business days, although any margin lending arrangement, transfer into a margin account or sale to meet a margin call is banned. The only route for a Designated Person would be the exceptional circumstances power, which purports to permit dealing 'in another way otherwise prohibited by this Policy' with the approval of the Company Secretary, the relevant Approver and sometimes the Remuneration Committee, but that sits in direct tension with the words 'in any circumstances' and is confined to matters such as severe financial hardship or a court order. For non-designated Personnel a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares is genuinely feasible, provided it is not a margin lending arrangement, has a tenor beyond three months and is not structured so as to look like a speculative bet on a price decrease, and is entered outside the four annual blackout periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Covered Persons are prohibited from: ... Using TechnologyOne's Securities as security for loans or margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, employee and contractor, with no approval or waiver route, so the funded structure cannot be offered.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked stock
bespoke_clauses.clause: Covered Persons are not permitted at any time to enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge their exposure to TechnologyOne securities which have not vested or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the loan ban, the hedging prohibition stops at unvested and locked shares, so an unfunded collar over vested unrestricted shares is not itself prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Securities" include shares, options, derivatives, and any other financial products of TechnologyOne that can be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The qualifier 'that can be traded on a financial market' leaves it arguable whether a bilateral OTC put and call are Securities at all, so the bank should assume they are and seek clearance rather than rely on the ambiguity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading (buying and selling Securities within a 3-month period).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities expressly include derivatives, buying a put and writing a call and then unwinding either leg inside three months risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading, so the collar tenor and any roll should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional blackout periods may be imposed by the Board or CEO as necessary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board or CEO can close the trading window without notice or stated criteria, so pricing, unwind or physical settlement of a collar can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all directors, officers, employees, and contractors of TechnologyOne and its subsidiaries (referred to as "Covered Persons").
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy never extends to spouses, dependants or controlled entities and trusts, so its literal reach over shares held through a family trust is untested rather than clearly prohibited; the bank should not treat that as a workaround.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Details of Trading in TechnologyOne Securities undertaken by the Chair, Directors or KMP are to be provided to the Company Secretary as soon as possible and within two business days of the Trade at the latest so that notification can be made via the ASX Announcements Platform.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll and unwind by a Director or KMP will be disclosed publicly through Appendix 3Y-style notification within two business days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chair, Directors and KMP are required to be granted approval from the following before Trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy states no validity period, response time, conditions power or revocation right for an approval, so the bank cannot rely on a defined execution window and should obtain the approval terms in writing before pricing.

TNE.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The derivative legs alone are workable over vested, unrestricted shares: the express hedging ban is confined to securities that have not vested or remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction, so a put and call over free shares is only 'Trading', requiring the Chair's prior approval for Directors and KMP (approval by the Audit & Risk Committee Chair and Managing Director for the Chair), execution in a Trading Window outside the 1 February, 1 March and 1 September blackouts, no Inside Information, and notification to the Company Secretary within two business days for ASX release. The loan leg is fatal: section 9 flatly prohibits every Covered Person from using TechnologyOne Securities as security for loans or margin lending, with no approval, tier or vesting carve-out, and the only exemption power (severe hardship or a court order) reaches blackout-period trading only. Because Securities expressly include derivatives, tenor and any roll or unwind should exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, and the Board or CEO can impose additional blackouts at any time. An unfunded collar is therefore available with clearance, but the bank cannot take security over the shares.

They may deal freely unless they hold inside information, have been formally notified that they are restricted, or are a Restricted Person.
