LNW.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chief Legal Officer may specify any other blackout period from time to time (for example while material non-public information is being assembled for release, or during a material event known only to a few directors or executives). Confidential: the existence of an event-specific blackout will not be announced other than to those aware of the triggering event and to Restricted Persons, and must not be disclosed to anyone else.

rules.detail: Absolute ban for every Employee and Connected Person on transactions in exchange-traded or other organised-market puts, calls or derivative securities over Company securities. No vesting distinction, no approval route and no exemption; section 5 excluded dealings disapply only sections 4.1 and 4.3.
rules.evidence: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.

rules.detail: A bilateral OTC put or call with a bank is not a 'publicly traded option' and so falls outside 3.4, but any OTC derivative that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities, or is designed to offset a decrease in their market price, is prohibited hedging under 3.5. The definition of securities expressly includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company, so an OTC option is itself a Company security and dealing in it by a Restricted Person would also require approval and fall in blackouts were it not already banned.
rules.evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on arrangements that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities. The policy draws no distinction between unvested, vested-but-locked and freely held securities, applies to Connected Persons, and provides no clearance or hardship route out of section 3.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities. You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named alongside hedging and banned outright, so a prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar cash-out structure is prohibited for all Employees irrespective of vesting or tier.
rules.evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Speculative dealing is banned and short selling is named as an instance of it; the policy defines short selling as borrowing and selling securities to buy them back lower.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers are additionally responsible for the statutory US restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities under Section 16 of the Exchange Act.
rules.evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities)

rules.detail: Lending out Company securities is never mentioned; borrowing securities appears only in the descriptive definition of short selling. The dealing definition (purchases, sales, gifts, donations, acquisitions, disposals and option exercises) does not sweep in a securities loan, although a lending arrangement that transferred title would be a disposal.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities is speculative dealing, is a derivative security if written on an organised market, and if short is both a hedge of a decrease in price and economically a short sale, so it is caught by three separate bans.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Holding Company securities in a margin account is prohibited for all Employees and Connected Persons. The only carve-out is the cashless exercise of options, where shares underlying the option are sold to fund tax, the exercise price and broker commissions.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: Pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan is expressly banned. A charge, lien or security interest unconnected with a loan is not named, and granting security is not part of the dealing definition, so it is only caught if it amounts to a pledge for a loan.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: Any loan collateralised by Company securities is prohibited, not merely a margin loan. The ban sits in section 3 (all Employees), has no tier or vesting carve-out, and is not among the section 5 excluded dealings, which relieve only the blackout and approval requirements in sections 4.1 and 4.3.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: No holding period or minimum interval is set. The restraint is qualitative: dealing on a speculative basis is banned, reinforced by the Front Page Test, and approval will not be granted where a dealing would fail that test.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers must comply with the US short-swing profit rule, under which profits on a purchase and sale (in either order) matched within six months are disgorgeable. This is imported by reference rather than being stated as a policy holding period.
rules.evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" ...) and Rule 144 of the Securities Act of 1933 in connection with their transactions in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Restricted Persons inherit every section 3 prohibition and add blackout periods and prior approval. Even if a derivative escaped sections 3.4 and 3.5, it would be a dealing in securities (the definition of securities includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company) requiring Chief Legal Officer approval and barred in the quarterly and event-specific blackouts.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Chief Legal Officer (or the CEO where the request is made by the Chief Legal Officer); the Chief Legal Officer may delegate and must do so if uncontactable for an extended period
clearance.evidence: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.

clearance.approver: Chief Legal Officer
clearance.post_trade_to: Chief Legal Officer (and Form 4 with the SEC)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered; Form 4 within two business days of most transactions
clearance.evidence: Following any trade, Directors and Section 16 Officers must promptly notify the Chief Legal Officer, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered.

clearance.approver: Chief Legal Officer
clearance.post_trade_to: Chief Legal Officer (and Form 4 with the SEC; Form 144 before certain open market sales)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered; Form 4 within two business days of most transactions
clearance.evidence: This includes filing a Form 4 with the SEC within two business days of most transactions in Company securities (including gifts), and filing a Form 144 prior to certain open market sale of Company shares.
Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

short_term.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

short_term.basis: US Exchange Act Section 16(b) short-swing profit matching, imported by reference for Directors and Section 16 Officers
short_term.evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits"

exceptions.approver: Chief Legal Officer (or CEO if the applicant is the Chief Legal Officer); waivers reported to the Board at the next scheduled board meeting
exceptions.evidence: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any Inside Information, then, they may apply for approval to deal. Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: Chief Legal Officer
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company, including: purchases of Company securities under the employee share purchase plan resulting from an employee's periodic payroll contributions; the exercise of a share option for cash; and the issuance of shares upon vesting of an award of restricted share units (RSUs)

acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of merger consideration, a scheme of arrangement or tender offer/equal access buy-back.

Dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary).

exceptions.approver: pre-approved; the plan must not be entered into or amended during a blackout
exceptions.evidence: Trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chief Legal Officer approves the steps taken by the donor
exceptions.evidence: Bona fide gifts of the Company's securities where the donor has taken appropriate steps approved by the Chief Legal Officer to ensure that the recipient will not sell the Company's securities while the donor is aware or in possession of Inside Information.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Standing orders are banned outright: 'You may not place standing orders (e.g. open orders at set prices) involving Company securities. A broker-executed standing order while you hold Inside Information may result in unlawful trading.' Price-triggered execution is therefore unavailable except under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan entered outside a blackout.

external_documents: Disclosure Policy
LNW.exemption_authority: Chief Legal Officer (CEO where the Chief Legal Officer is the applicant) may approve a Restricted Person's dealing during a blackout in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or court order, on sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action; waivers are reported to the Board at its next scheduled meeting. There is no exemption authority at all for the section 3 prohibitions (speculative dealing, publicly traded options, hedging, monetisation, standing orders, margin accounts and pledging): section 5 excluded dealings disapply only sections 4.1 and 4.3.
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities law: Exchange Act Section 16 (short-swing profit disgorgement, short sale restrictions, Form 4 within two business days), Rule 144 and Form 144, Regulation FD, and 'material non-public information' read as equivalent to Inside Information

Australian law: Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) insider trading provisions and the ASX Listing Rules; the blackout end anchor requires a full trading day on both the ASX and a US national securities exchange

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to the following: ... [excluded dealings]. Exceptional circumstances relief in section 4.2 is likewise expressed as relief to 'deal in securities during a blackout period'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every relief mechanism in the policy operates only on the blackout and approval requirements, so the hedging, monetisation, publicly traded options and pledging bans that kill a funded collar cannot be waived by anyone, including the Board.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put leg of a collar is the paradigm arrangement designed to offset a decrease in market price, and the word 'monetisation' independently captures the funded element, so the structure is prohibited on its face for all Employees and Connected Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is separately and expressly prohibited, so even an unfunded collar could not be financed against the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Listed puts and calls are barred outright, and while a bilateral bank OTC option is not 'publicly traded', the substance over form statement means the Company will look through an OTC wrapper used to achieve the same result.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A structure engineered to sit outside the literal words (for example a bespoke OTC collar, a Connected Person entity, or a non-recourse loan documented as a sale) will still be assessed on its economic substance as hedging or monetisation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a dealing that is technically permitted must survive a reputational test, and a bank-funded collar over executive shares is precisely the kind of transaction that would fail it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not place standing orders (e.g. open orders at set prices) involving Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Price-triggered or knock-in/knock-out features and automatic delivery mechanics would need to be recast as a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, which cannot be entered into or amended during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities when the Employee to whom they are connected would be permitted to do so under this Policy. The same restrictions that apply to Employees apply equally to their Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a controlled trust, household member or influenced family member does not escape any of the prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of 'short-swing profits' and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For US-reporting insiders the put and call legs are themselves Section 16 derivative securities: entering, amending or settling them creates reportable transactions that can be matched against ordinary purchases within six months, generating disgorgement risk independent of the ASX policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved leg of a multi-step structure can be pulled without reasons before execution, and the five business day approval life means a cleared trade must be priced and closed quickly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can extinguish the very shares that collateralise the bank's loan, so the bank's security is exposed to a disciplinary outcome rather than only market risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are aware of Inside Information when your employment or engagement ends, you must not trade until that information becomes public and one full trading day has elapsed, or it ceases to be material.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Departure does not immediately free an executive to enter or unwind a structure, though the section 3 bans are framed as applying to Employees and so would fall away on cessation.

LNW.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy at any tier or vesting state. Section 3.5 expressly prohibits every Employee, Director, consultant and Connected Person from entering hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities, which captures the purchased put and the collar as a whole, and separately prohibits holding Company securities in a margin account or pledging them as collateral for a loan, which kills the secured loan leg. Section 3.4 independently bans transactions in publicly traded puts, calls and derivative securities on an exchange or any other organised market, and although a bilateral OTC option with a bank is not literally 'publicly traded', the Company's stated substance over form approach and the Front Page Test mean an OTC wrapper achieving the same economics would still be treated as a breach. None of these prohibitions can be waived: the exceptional circumstances relief in section 4.2 and the excluded dealings in section 5 disapply only the section 4.1 blackout and the section 4.3 approval requirement, so there is no exemption authority for section 3 and no hardship route. For US-reporting Directors and Section 16 Officers, the option legs would in any event be reportable derivative securities exposed to short-swing profit disgorgement and the statutory short sale restrictions.

GMD.title: Securities Trading Policy (GMD-CORP-POL-1004)

tiers.name: Restricted Persons

GMD.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board (or its delegate) may impose an Additional Period from time to time, for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure but for ASX Listing Rule 3.1A. It applies in addition to the Blackout Periods and is confidential: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps, futures and hedges, whether cash settled or not, and Dealing expressly includes granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation. Buying a put from a bank and writing a call to it are therefore each a Dealing in Company Securities: permitted outside Prohibited Periods with prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer. If the derivative is protective it must additionally clear Section 7.3.
rules.evidence: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company, and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options, and derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, share warrants and similar instruments are named as prohibited where they are short term or speculative. A long-dated, non-speculative exchange-traded derivative is not caught by 7.2 and would fall back to being a Dealing requiring clearance, but the qualifier is applied by the Approving Officer together with the front page test.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities, including derivative market transactions involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Any derivative that operates as a protection arrangement over unvested Company Securities, or securities subject to a holding lock, is banned outright with no clearance route. Derivatives that are not protective remain Dealings requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Absolute ban, at any time, on protection arrangements over unvested Company Securities; the definition reaches securities held beneficially on the Restricted Person's behalf, for example in trust or under an incentive plan. No Approving Officer discretion is available.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or holding term (for example performance-based remuneration not yet released) are treated identically to unvested securities: protection arrangements over them are prohibited at any time. Release from the holding lock is itself an excluded dealing, after which the vested_unrestricted rule applies.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: For securities that are neither unvested nor subject to a holding lock, a protection arrangement is expressly permitted subject to approval under Section 6: prior written request to the relevant Approving Officer copied to the Company Secretary, written clearance valid five business days and withdrawable, outside Blackout Periods and any Additional Period, and satisfying the front page test.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: ... and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar cash-out over vested unrestricted securities is a protection arrangement (it limits the economic risk of the holding) requiring approval under Section 6, and if it is secured on the securities the loan leg separately requires clearance under 7.4. Over unvested or holding-lock securities the same structure is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf

rules.detail: Short selling is listed as a species of protection arrangement, so it is banned outright in respect of unvested or holding-lock securities.
rules.evidence: "protection arrangements" include transactions which: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities

rules.detail: Unusually, the policy does not ban short selling outright. Because it is drafted as a protection arrangement, short selling of securities that are not unvested or holding-locked 'otherwise requires approval under Section 6'. In practice a short sale would be speculative trading contrary to 7.2 and would fail the front page test, so clearance should not be expected.

A stock loan that transferred title would be a disposal and so a Dealing, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for difference are named in the speculative trading ban. The prohibition is qualified by the words 'which are short term or speculative', and a short CFD would independently be a protection arrangement enabling profit from a price decrease, prohibited over unvested or holding-lock securities and otherwise requiring Section 6 approval.

rules.detail: The clause is not confined to margin loans: 'or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities' captures a bank loan secured on collared shares. rules.detail: Qualitative ban with no stated holding period or matching window: short-term or speculative trading is prohibited 'under no circumstances', expressly extending to derivative market transactions that are short term or speculative.

GMD.exemption_authority: The Approving Officer determined under the Section 6 table may grant Disposal Consent during a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or court enforceable undertaking, other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or other circumstances deemed exceptional by the Approving Officer). That consent extends only to disposing of or transferring securities, expressly 'not to acquire or otherwise Deal with' them. There is no waiver power over the Section 7.3 ban on protection arrangements for unvested or holding-locked securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of 'protection arrangements' for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the pivotal clause: a collar is permissible in principle over vested, lock-free shares with clearance, but is absolutely barred over unvested awards and vested shares still under a holding lock, so the collateral pool must be carefully segregated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this does not ban secured financing, so the funded leg of the collar is available on approval, but the loan and the derivative legs each need clearance and both must be obtained before the structure is entered into.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (for example, under a margin lending arrangement) [is excluded from the blackout restrictions] ... Unless otherwise stated, prior written clearance under Section 6 is not required for the above Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank can enforce its security and sell the collared shares during a Blackout Period or Additional Period without putting the executive in breach and without a fresh clearance, which materially de-risks the lending leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee plan trust or a family trust count towards the hedging test, so a structure written over trust-held shares needs the same approval and, if those shares are still locked, is prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for a period of five business days ... Written clearance under this policy may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... should the Approving Officer consider that circumstances have changed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documenting and executing both the derivative and the loan must fit inside a five business day window that the Company can revoke at will, so the bank should expect signing risk up to the moment of execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approving Officer may as appropriate, seek input from relevant Key Management Personnel and Senior Employees about the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing ... Where any approval under this policy is required for a dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the "front page" test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for an executive collar is a discretionary reputational judgment rather than a mechanical check, and the front page test is an express bar on approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no acquisition relief in a blackout
bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given prior written clearance to dispose of or transfer (but not to acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even in hardship, a collar cannot be entered, rolled or restructured during a Blackout or Additional Period; only outright disposals or transfers can be cleared, so timing must fall in an open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing ... involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar, or one with early termination or knock-out features, risks being characterised as short-term derivative dealing prohibited 'under no circumstances', so tenor and structure should be plainly long-term and protective.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person is: ... a Connected Person of any person referred to in the sub-paragraphs above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A spouse, controlled company or family trust entering the collar or the loan is itself a Restricted Person needing its own clearance, so nothing is gained by moving the structure off the executive's own name.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC and cash-settled derivatives are securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities ... includes ... derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cash-settled OTC collar cannot be argued to fall outside the policy on the basis that no shares move; it is a dealing in Company Securities in its own right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary must maintain a register of notifications and clearances given in relation to trading in Company Securities ... and must report all notifications ... upon request by the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approval of a collar and secured loan will be recorded and reportable to the Board, and for directors the resulting change of interest is disclosed to ASX within five business days.

GMD.summary: A funded collar is possible for a Genesis Restricted Person, but only over Company Securities that are neither unvested nor subject to a holding lock, and only with two prior written clearances. Section 7.3 prohibits protection arrangements 'at any time' over unvested or holding-locked securities but otherwise routes them to Section 6 approval, and section 7.4 does not ban secured financing at all: margin loans and other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities simply require prior written clearance from the Approving Officer set by the Section 6 table (Chair for the MD & CEO and executive directors, MD & CEO for the Chair and non-director KMP, both jointly for other non-executive directors, Company Secretary or CFO for everyone else). Entry, roll or unwind must occur outside the four Blackout Periods running from 20 March, 20 June, 20 September and 20 December and outside any confidential Additional Period, must be executed within the five business days that clearance remains valid, and can be withdrawn at any time before execution on reputational or governance grounds or if it fails the front page test. Helpfully for the bank, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is an excluded dealing needing no clearance and permitted during a Prohibited Period, so enforcement does not breach the policy. The main structuring constraints are the ban on short-term or speculative derivative dealing in section 7.2, which argues for a long tenor and no speculative features, and the fact that hardship relief in a blackout extends only to disposals and never to entering a new arrangement.

tiers.name: Sonic Employees

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: transactions in products which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements or entitlements subject to a holding lock under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive limit: the hedging prohibition does not reach vested, unlocked shares, so a collar over those shares is not banned, but the collateral pool must exclude anything still unvested or under a holding lock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors of Sonic Healthcare Limited are also prohibited from entering into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities without the prior approval of the Chair (and for the Chair, the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee) and disclosure of such arrangements to the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is available to a director on Chair approval plus Board disclosure rather than being prohibited, and the clause binds directors only, so non-director Designated Officers face no secured financing restriction at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers are only permitted to trade in the period of eight weeks commencing on the business day after the public announcement of half year and year end results ... The Sonic Board of Directors must specifically consider and approve the opening of the "trading window" in each instance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime: outside a Board-approved window a Designated Officer simply cannot trade, so entry, roll, restrike or unwind of a collar must be scheduled into a window that the Board has actually opened.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers are required to commit to this by signing the Securities Trading Policy and will forfeit their equity rewards should they be found to be in breach.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can extinguish the executive's unvested equity, which both removes future collateral and creates a strong incentive to structure conservatively; a bank should not lend against awards that a policy breach could forfeit.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: ... short-term trading and short selling arrangements in Sonic securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no defined period, a short-dated or early-terminable collar risks being characterised as a short-term trading arrangement, so tenor should be clearly long and the structure should not contain features that look like a synthetic short.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sonic securities (including shares, options, derivatives, debt securities and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market) ... The prohibitions described above also apply to trading in financial products issued or created over Sonic's securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The core definition is limited to products tradeable on a financial market, but the extension sentence sweeps in bilateral bank-created products over Sonic securities, so an OTC collar cannot be argued outside the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any clearance to trade can be given or refused by the appropriate person in their discretion, without giving any reasons; a clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; ... a decision to refuse clearance is final and binding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Where approval is needed (Chair approval for secured financing, or for a sale by the Managing Director or Finance Director) it is unreviewable and revocable up to execution, so the bank carries signing risk on the funded leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sonic's Chair or Managing Director may impose other periods when Designated Officers are prohibited from trading because price sensitive, non-public information may exist.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open window can be shut at short notice without any stated disclosure obligation, which can strand a partially executed or maturing structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All Sonic share dealings by Directors must be promptly notified to the ASX by the Company Secretary. Directors are therefore required to complete an Appendix 3Y and forward to the Company Secretary within two business days of executing (i.e. before settlement) any trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both derivative legs and any change in the nature of a director's interest arising from the collar and the security will become public via the Appendix 3Y within two business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In relation to any person under (a) to (d) above: their spouse ... their nominee, including an investment manager managing funds on their behalf; a trust of which they, or any of their connected persons ... are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which they or any of their connected persons ... control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar booked in a family trust, controlled company or through a discretionary investment manager is treated as the Designated Officer's own trade and must sit in a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Version Date: 4 November 2016.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an old policy that predates the market convention of banning all hedging by KMP; the absence of a general hedging ban should be confirmed against the current remuneration report and any equity plan rules before a bank relies on it.

SHL.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, and Sonic is unusually permissive by current ASX standards. The hedging prohibition in 2.2 reaches only products that limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements or entitlements subject to a holding lock under an equity based remuneration scheme, so a put and call over fully vested, unlocked shares is not prohibited; it is simply trading in a product created over Sonic securities, which a Designated Officer may do only inside a Board-approved trading window (eight weeks after half year and year end results, five weeks after the AGM, two weeks after specific guidance), free of inside information, with trade details to the Company Secretary within 24 hours and, for directors, an Appendix 3Y within two business days. The secured loan leg is likewise permitted rather than banned: a director must obtain the prior approval of the Chair (the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee if the applicant is the Chair) and disclose the arrangement to the Board, while non-director Designated Officers face no secured financing restriction at all. The principal constraints are the narrow windows, which can be closed at any time by the Chair or Managing Director, the undefined prohibition on short-term trading and short selling arrangements, which argues for a long tenor and no synthetic short features, and the forfeiture of equity rewards that follows any breach. Because the policy dates from 2016 and the equity plan rules are not before us, the vesting and holding-lock status of every share pledged should be verified before the structure is entered.

rules.detail: Derivatives are never named. The definition of Securities lists shares, debentures, units or other interests in a scheme, options over unissued shares or units, and rights to subscribe: it does not include options or other derivatives written by third parties over issued GPT Securities. Dealing is confined to selling, otherwise disposing of or acquiring GPT Securities (or arranging someone else to do so) and transferring legal ownership. A bank-written OTC put or call over existing stapled securities therefore falls outside both definitions unless it hedges restricted remuneration or is part of a secured financing, and physical settlement would be a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and notification.
A put, collar or other derivative that limits exposure to risk on an unvested element of remuneration is banned outright with no window or clearance route, whatever the venue.
rules.evidence: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging or any arrangement limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration. No exemption, hardship or Board waiver is provided: section 9 relief runs only to selling or disposing of Securities outside a window.
rules.evidence: KMPs and Employees are prohibited from: ... hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: Remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a trading restriction (holding lock or holding term) or a forfeiture condition is treated identically to unvested remuneration; hedging it is prohibited until the restriction and forfeiture condition fall away.
rules.evidence: an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is drafted by reference to remuneration that is unvested or still restricted, so it does not reach securities that have fully vested with no trading restriction or forfeiture condition, nor securities bought on market. Such a hedge is not prohibited, but it must not involve any security interest or secured financing over GPT Securities, must not be speculative or short-term, and any resulting acquisition, disposal or transfer of legal ownership must occur in a Trading Window after notification of intention to deal.
rules.evidence: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such, but any monetisation that raises money against GPT Securities is caught: the fourth bullet of 5.2 bans margin loans using GPT Securities as security and 'any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities' without qualification as to vesting or tier. Only a wholly unsecured hedge over fully vested, unrestricted securities escapes.
rules.evidence: obtaining margin loans using GPT Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling GPT securities is named as a form of prohibited speculative dealing, banned at all times including within a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: KMPs and Employees are prohibited from: engaging in speculative dealing in GPT securities, being short-selling GPT securities and short-term dealing

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned. The Dealing definition covers disposals, acquisitions and transfers of legal ownership, so a stock loan transferring title would be a Dealing needing a Trading Window and notification, but the policy does not address lending as such.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over GPT securities is speculative dealing and, if short, is economically a short sale; either characterisation is prohibited. A long CFD is not a Security under the definition and so is not otherwise regulated.
rules.evidence: engaging in speculative dealing in GPT securities, being short-selling GPT securities and short-term dealing

rules.detail: Margin loans secured on GPT Securities are banned, whether the securities stand alone or form part of a wider portfolio. No approval, hardship or grandfathering route is offered and the ban applies to KMP, Employees and, through section 2, their Associates.
rules.evidence: obtaining margin loans using GPT Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans

rules.detail: A dedicated bullet prohibits granting a security interest in respect of vested GPT Securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, whatever the purpose of the financial arrangement.
rules.evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested GPT Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: For fully vested, unrestricted securities the security interest bullet does not apply, but the following bullet does: any secured financing arrangement in respect of GPT Securities is prohibited, so a charge or pledge to a lender is caught. A security interest granted otherwise than in connection with financing is not addressed and is not itself a Dealing.
rules.evidence: or entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any secured financing arrangement in respect of GPT Securities, extending well beyond margin lending. It is unqualified as to tier, vesting state, quantum or lender, there is no approval route, and the section 9 exceptional circumstances power is confined to selling or disposing of Securities.
rules.evidence: or entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities.

rules.detail: A hard 30 day rule: buying and then selling (or selling and then buying) any GPT securities within 30 days is prohibited short-term dealing, regardless of profit or intention. The only carve-out is for Securities acquired on the exercise or vesting of Securities under a GPT employee incentive scheme.
rules.evidence: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) GPT securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any GPT securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing). The exception to this is regarding Securities acquired on the exercise or vesting of Securities under any GPT employee incentive scheme

GPT.exemption_authority: Section 9 permits a KMP or Employee who needs to sell or dispose of GPT Securities outside a Trading Window in exceptional circumstances to apply in writing to the General Counsel and Company Secretary (to the CEO where the applicant is the General Counsel and Company Secretary), to the Chairman in the case of Directors, and to the Chairman of the Audit Committee in the case of the Chairman. It requires sufficient evidence that selling or disposing is the most reasonable course of action and a declaration of no inside information, and the approver may deny or impose conditions without reasons. The power extends only to selling or disposing of Securities: there is no authority to waive the section 5.2 prohibitions on hedging, security interests, margin loans or other secured financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMPs and Employees are prohibited from ... obtaining margin loans using GPT Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is decisive: the loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared securities, is prohibited outright for every KMP, Employee and Associate with no vesting carve-out and no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: security interest over restricted vested securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested GPT Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a financing that was not otherwise 'secured financing' cannot take a security interest over vested securities still under a holding lock or forfeiture condition, so no part of the restricted holding can be pledged.

bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is tied to restricted remuneration, so an unfunded collar over fully vested, unrestricted securities is not itself banned; only the funding and security elements are.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: Includes: shares or debentures in a company or unit or other interest in a scheme; an option over an unissued share, or debenture of, the company; ... Dealing: To: Sell (or otherwise dispose) or acquire GPT Securities or arrange someone else to do so whether on or off market; and Transfer legal ownership of Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Third-party derivatives over issued GPT Securities are not within the defined terms, so an OTC option is regulated only through the hedging and secured financing bullets, while any physical settlement is squarely a Dealing needing a Trading Window and notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) GPT securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any GPT securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A mechanical matching rule with no intention element: any share purchase or sale within 30 days on either side of a physically settled leg breaches the policy, so settlement timing must be mapped against all other dealings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMPs, Employees and Associates are prohibited from dealing in GPT Securities during all periods that are outside an available trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime with five six-week windows a year, so entry, settlement or unwind of any structure must be scheduled inside a window that has not been suspended.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The availability of any Trading Window may be varied, suspended or terminated by the GPT Group Board at any time, including being varied for all KMP and Employees or a subset of persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board can close a window for one individual without notice to the market, which can strand a partially executed structure or block a scheduled settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Receipt of a notification of intention to deal and any clearance provided is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not endorsement or approval of the proposed dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot treat a GPT clearance as company approval of the structure; the executive bears full responsibility and a clearance carries no comfort that the arrangement complies with 5.2.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any breach of this Policy or failure to act within the spirit of this Policy will be viewed seriously and will be subject to disciplinary action which may include termination of employment with GPT.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring around the literal words of the secured financing ban, for example through a non-recourse prepaid forward or a third-party funder, would still be judged against the spirit of the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: extends to a KMP's and an Employee's family, related parties or associates, including related corporations, superannuation funds or investment vehicles where the KMP or Employee has influence over the related parties' judgement in relation to investment decisions
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust, controlled company or self-managed fund does not avoid the secured financing prohibition or the window restriction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance provided under this section must be effected (even if not settled) within five business days of the date of the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any dealing leg must be executed within five business days of notification, and the approver may impose conditions in their discretion without giving reasons.

GPT.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 5.2 prohibits KMP, Employees and their Associates from obtaining margin loans using GPT Securities as security and from entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities, an unqualified ban with no vesting carve-out, no approval route and no waiver power, so the loan leg secured on the collared securities is prohibited outright. A separate bullet bans granting a security interest over vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, and hedging is prohibited for any element of remuneration that is unvested or still restricted. The unfunded derivative legs over fully vested, unrestricted securities are not themselves banned, and indeed sit largely outside the narrow definitions of Securities and Dealing, but any physical settlement, and any acquisition or disposal in connection with the structure, must occur inside one of the five six-week Trading Windows, must be preceded by a notification of intention to deal to the applicable approver (Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman, Chairman of the Board for other Directors, the CEO for the Executive Team, the General Counsel & Company Secretary for everyone else), must be effected within five business days of clearance, and must not fall within 30 days of any other buy or sell. Section 9 relief is confined to selling or disposing of Securities in exceptional circumstances and cannot authorise any part of the financing.

CHC.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Charter Hall may declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts in Securities at any time at its absolute discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary. Trading Windows otherwise operate automatically, and the Group Company Secretary notifies Directors and Employees by email when a Trading Window starts or closes. Consent may also be refused, without reasons, when management accounts are available at a time other than during a Trading Window.

rules.detail: Directional asymmetry is the key feature: a derivative position over vested securities, or securities held outside an incentive scheme, may only be bought, only during a Trading Window and only with the Chair's consent, while selling (writing) a derivative position is prohibited outright. A purchased put is therefore available; the written call leg of a collar is not. OTC instruments are squarely within the definition of Securities, which covers swaps, contracts for differences, options and other derivatives over or related to the performance of Charter Hall securities, and interests created over those securities by third parties.
rules.evidence: In relation to vested Securities (held within a Group employee incentive scheme) or Securities held outside such a scheme: 1. you can only buy a derivative position during a trading window, and 2. you cannot sell a derivative position.

rules.detail: Same buy-only rule for exchange-traded options and warrants, which are within the definition of Securities. An Employee needs the Managing Director & Group CEO's consent unless the transaction is a single Dealing not exceeding $20,000, and every trade must be raised in Resolver regardless.
rules.evidence: you can only buy a derivative position during a trading window, and 2. you cannot sell a derivative position.

rules.detail: Any transaction or arrangement hedging exposure to the price of unvested Securities, or Securities subject to a holding lock, is banned outright; no consent, window or special circumstances route is available.
rules.evidence: You cannot enter, or seek to enter any type of transaction or arrangement that would hedge the exposure to movements in the price of unvested Securities or those which remain subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging unvested Securities, expressed to catch even seeking to enter such an arrangement. Applies equally to Directors and Employees and to Dealings through nominees, family members, companies or trusts.
rules.evidence: Hedging of Securities is not allowed. You cannot enter, or seek to enter any type of transaction or arrangement that would hedge the exposure to movements in the price of unvested Securities or those which remain subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Securities that remain subject to a holding lock are treated exactly like unvested Securities, so vested but locked incentive securities cannot be hedged or collared until the lock is released.
rules.evidence: any type of transaction or arrangement that would hedge the exposure to movements in the price of unvested Securities or those which remain subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Hedging vested Securities and Securities held outside an incentive scheme is permitted only within three constraints: the position may only be bought and never sold, it may only be bought during a Trading Window (with consent from the respective Chair for Directors or the Managing Director & Group CEO for Employees), and the arrangement must remain in the holder's own control rather than a third party's. A protective put therefore qualifies; a collar, which requires writing a call and typically places control of settlement and enforcement with the bank, does not.
rules.evidence: The only hedging arrangements allowed is when they are in your control, rather than the control of any third party. In taking out such approved positions, you must adhere to this Policy at all times.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Every mechanism by which it is achieved is blocked: a collar or prepaid forward requires selling a derivative position, which is prohibited; a share-backed facility is a margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, which is prohibited; and the hedge would be in the control of a third party rather than the holder.
rules.evidence: you cannot sell a derivative position. The only hedging arrangements allowed is when they are in your control, rather than the control of any third party.

rules.detail: Short selling of the stapled securities is not named. A synthetic short is expressly caught because it requires selling a derivative position. An outright physical short would also be inconsistent with the stated purpose of encouraging long term holding and with the four-week rule against selling recently acquired Securities, but the policy contains no express prohibition.
rules.evidence: you cannot sell a derivative position.

rules.detail: Securities lending or borrowing is nowhere mentioned, and the Dealing definition (buying and selling, exercising or executing financial instruments, agreeing to buy or sell, procuring, communicating) does not capture a stock loan unless it involves a sale.

Contracts for differences are expressly listed as Securities, so they are governed by the derivative position rule: a long CFD may be bought during a Trading Window with consent, while a short CFD is a sold derivative position and is prohibited. A CFD closed out within four weeks would also breach the short-term trading rule.
rules.evidence: Securities: Stapled securities, shares, quoted (i.e. listed) units, debt securities and other financial instruments, issued by Charter Hall or any interest created over those securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, future contracts, contracts for differences, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of those securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on entering, or seeking to enter, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, whether the Securities stand alone or form part of a wider investment portfolio. No consent, hardship or special circumstances route is offered, and the ban is not limited by vesting state or tier.
rules.evidence: You are not allowed to enter into, or seek to enter into, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, whether on a stand-alone basis or as part of an investment portfolio.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Charter Hall Securities is not mentioned and is not within the Dealing definition. It is regulated only indirectly: if the security supports a margin loan arrangement it is prohibited by 2.5, and a third party holding enforcement rights over the securities would take the hedge outside the holder's own control contrary to 2.4.

The policy names only margin loans, not secured financing generally. However the ban is drafted as 'any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities', which on its natural reading captures a bank facility secured on Charter Hall Securities with loan-to-value maintenance, the structure used to fund a collar. A fixed-term facility secured on the securities with no margining is not expressly addressed, but would still require the holder to cede control of the hedged securities to a third party contrary to 2.4.
rules.evidence: You are not allowed to enter into, or seek to enter into, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, whether on a stand-alone basis or as part of an investment portfolio.

rules.detail: Selling Securities within four weeks of the date of acquisition is prohibited, subject only to the Employee Security Plans carve-out. Separately, Employees may not use the $20,000 no-consent concession to run up Dealings exceeding $20,000 within a 30-day period without consent; breaches are investigated by Risk and Compliance from the Resolver records.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading of Securities (i.e., selling Securities within a four-week period from the date of acquisition) is not allowed, except in the circumstances outlined under 'Employee Security Plans'.

The restrictions in this Policy do not prevent you from accepting a takeover bid or from selling Securities under a scheme of arrangement in respect of Charter Hall.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In relation to vested Securities (held within a Group employee incentive scheme) or Securities held outside such a scheme: 1. you can only buy a derivative position during a trading window, and 2. you cannot sell a derivative position.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause defeats a collar: the written call is a sold derivative position and is prohibited outright, even over fully vested securities, while the purchased put on its own would be permissible in a window with consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedge must stay in your control
bespoke_clauses.clause: The only hedging arrangements allowed is when they are in your control, rather than the control of any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-documented OTC structure with dealer election rights, early termination triggers or enforcement over the shares places control with a third party, so even a put-only hedge must be structured so the executive retains control.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are not allowed to enter into, or seek to enter into, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, whether on a stand-alone basis or as part of an investment portfolio.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funded leg is blocked: 'any type of margin loan arrangement' naturally covers a share-backed facility with loan-to-value maintenance, and the prohibition extends to merely seeking to enter one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 2.5 addresses margin loans only; the policy contains no prohibition on secured financing generally and no clause making the grant of a security interest a Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A term loan secured on Charter Hall Securities without margining sits in a genuine gap in the drafting, but it would still fall foul of the control requirement in 2.4 and should be cleared with the Company Secretary rather than assumed permissible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You cannot enter, or seek to enter any type of transaction or arrangement that would hedge the exposure to movements in the price of unvested Securities or those which remain subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collateral pool must exclude unvested awards and vested securities still under a holding lock; the prohibition bites on attempting the arrangement, not just completing it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading of Securities (i.e., selling Securities within a four-week period from the date of acquisition) is not allowed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Securities delivered or acquired in connection with a structure cannot be sold for four weeks, which constrains delivery mechanics and any unwind that involves selling recently acquired securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a trade is set to trigger at a set price and has not been completed within the 5 business days a new consent will need to be obtained. If the trade has not happened and the window is closing, this trade must be cancelled by the end of business day of the close of a trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Contingent or price-triggered execution cannot survive a window close, so knock-in or barrier features that execute automatically are incompatible with the consent regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading Windows to Deal in Securities are as follows: 1. for the period beginning the day after the announcement of the Charter Hall Group's half year results until and including 31 May; and 2. for the period beginning the day after the announcement of the Charter Hall Group's annual results until and including 30 November.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only two windows a year, each ending on a fixed calendar date, so any entry, roll or unwind must be scheduled well before 31 May or 30 November.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Charter Hall may declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts in Securities at any time at its absolute discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A window can be closed without warning, and consent may be withheld without reasons whenever management accounts are available outside a window, so execution certainty is low.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent will not be given if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached by the Dealing. Consent may not be given when management accounts are available at a time other than during a Trading Window. Furthermore, no reason is required to be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'any possibility' standard is deliberately conservative, so an approver is likely to refuse a structure whose compliance is arguable, and there is no appeal or reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: ... any interest created over those securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, future contracts, contracts for differences, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of those securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-created OTC option or swap over Charter Hall securities is itself a Security, so every leg is a Dealing subject to windows, consent and the notification regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Charter Hall must disclose any purchase or sale of listed Securities by any one of its Directors to the ASX within 5 business days from the Dealing being settled/completed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted derivative purchase by a director becomes public within five business days of settlement, so the structure cannot be kept confidential.

CHC.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 2.4 permits a hedge over vested, unlocked securities only in one direction: a derivative position may be bought during a Trading Window with consent, but 'you cannot sell a derivative position', so the written call leg of a collar is prohibited outright, and the further requirement that any permitted hedging arrangement be 'in your control, rather than the control of any third party' is incompatible with a bank-documented structure carrying dealer election and enforcement rights. Section 2.5 separately bans entering, or seeking to enter, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, which on its natural reading covers a facility secured on the collared securities; there is no general secured financing clause, so a non-margining term loan is not expressly addressed but would still offend the control requirement. Hedging is prohibited absolutely for unvested Securities and for vested Securities still subject to a holding lock. What remains available is an unfunded protective put over fully vested, unlocked holdings, bought inside one of the two annual Trading Windows (from the day after half year results to 31 May, and from the day after annual results to 30 November), with consent from the respective Chair for a Director, executed within five business days, notified to the Company Secretary within two business days and disclosed to the ASX within five business days of settlement.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Cochlear Securities are expressly permitted, and 'Derivative' expressly includes caps and/or collars and any structure intended to limit economic risk, with no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank qualifies. rules.detail: Absolute ban on any use of Derivatives in relation to unvested Cochlear Securities, extended to Associates. Securities issued subject to a holding lock are treated as unvested until the lock is released, so vested-but-locked shares cannot be collared either.

rules.evidence: Subject to the Act and this Policy (including Sections 4.3, 4.5 and Section 9), the use of Derivatives in relation to vested Cochlear Securities is permitted.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but fall within Derivatives under section 761D of the Act and within the catch-all for structures limiting economic risk, so entry is a Dealing subject to windows and clearance. A short CFD would in substance breach the short selling ban.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted subject to the ordinary Dealing regime: entry into a Margin Lending Arrangement is a Dealing, so it must occur in a Trading Window (with a 'no objection' notice for Key Designated Persons) or under a waiver. rules.detail: Using Cochlear Securities as collateral, or granting security over them, is expressly a Dealing rather than a prohibited act, so a pledge to a bank is permitted if made in a Trading Window with the required clearance.

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing. Any use of Securities as collateral is a Dealing requiring compliance with Section 4.3, and the policy contemplates secured lending by exempting a secured lender's involuntary enforcement sale provided the Policy was complied with at entry.
rules.evidence: An involuntary disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example under a Margin Lending Arrangement (provided that this Policy was complied with (where it was required to be complied with) in relation to entry into the relevant secured lending arrangement)

rules.detail: The policy does not expressly address pledging unvested Plan Awards or holding-locked securities as collateral. Section 4.5 bars only arrangements limiting economic risk of unvested remuneration, which a pledge alone does not obviously do.

Section 9 is headed 'Short Term and Speculative Dealing' but imposes no holding period, no minimum tenor and no intention test; it contains only an exhortation to be long term holders, followed by the short selling and stock lending bans.
