bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative includes: derivatives within the meaning of section 761D of the Act, such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants and caps and/or collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates collars as a recognised instrument and, over vested unlocked shares, permits them, so the derivative legs are squarely within the permitted category rather than an unaddressed structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: collateral is a dealing, not a prohibition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or Dealing includes ... the use of Securities as collateral or security over Securities (including a Margin Lending Arrangement).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The secured loan leg is permitted but must itself be timed inside a Trading Window and, for a Key Designated Person, covered by a notice of 'no objection'; the pledge and the option legs should be cleared together.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An involuntary disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example under a Margin Lending Arrangement (provided that this Policy was complied with ... in relation to entry into the relevant secured lending arrangement), is an Exempt Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank may enforce its security or close out the collar in a Prohibited Period without putting the executive in breach, provided the facility was properly cleared at inception - a materially better enforcement position than most ASX policies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Cochlear Security (including where applicable any Plan Award) that is issued subject to a holding lock shall (notwithstanding any vesting) be subject to the same restrictions under this Section 4.5 as unvested Cochlear Securities, until the holding lock is released.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only vested shares free of any holding lock may be collared, so the bank must diligence the lock status of each parcel and not merely its vesting.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no objection expires with the window
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a notice of "no objection" is given, the Key Designated Person must execute the proposed Dealing before the end of the Trading Window during which the notice of "no objection" was given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and settlement of the collar and the loan must all complete inside a 30 day window that the Company Secretary can terminate early at any time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Cochlear may by notice in writing to a Designated Person withdraw a notice of "no objection" or waiver of this Policy if, subsequent to the grant, new information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances. Upon withdrawal ... the relevant Designated Person must not carry out any Dealings ... that remain unexecuted at the time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should treat clearance as revocable up to execution and avoid staged or delayed closings that could be caught by a withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary may end a Trading Window immediately by notice in writing to Designated Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinds, rolls, resets and top-ups of the collar can be blocked without warning, so the documentation should allow cash settlement or lender-side action that falls within the secured lender exemption.

bespoke_clauses.topic: unvested hedging ban extends to associates
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not enter (and must procure that none of his or her Associates enter) into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration (including any Plan Award) that has not vested.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The structure cannot be routed through a spouse, controlled company or family trust to hedge unvested awards, and the 'with anyone' wording captures OTC arrangements with a bank.

bespoke_clauses.topic: disclosure of derivative and financing positions
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors of Cochlear must disclose to Cochlear any Derivatives position relating to Cochlear Securities. If requested by Cochlear, a Designated Person must disclose to Cochlear details of their current Derivatives positions [and] Margin Lending Arrangements relating to Cochlear Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the collar and the secured loan are disclosable to the company and potentially to the ASX, so confidentiality of the trade terms cannot be assured.

bespoke_clauses.topic: short selling and stock lending bans
bespoke_clauses.clause: Cochlear Personnel must not engage in short selling or stock lending activities in relation to Cochlear Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive must deliver or pledge shares they own outright and cannot lend stock to the bank to support its hedge, so the bank must hedge its own delta in the market.

COH.summary: A funded collar is workable at Cochlear and this is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the structure. Section 4.5 expressly permits the use of Derivatives, a term defined to include caps and collars, in relation to vested Cochlear Securities, and the Dealing definition treats the use of securities as collateral and entry into a Margin Lending Arrangement as permitted Dealings rather than prohibited acts, so both the option legs and the secured loan are available. The conditions are that the shares are vested and free of any holding lock (holding-locked shares are treated as unvested and cannot be hedged), that the whole transaction is executed within a Trading Window - the 30 days after half or full year results or after the AGM - and that a Key Designated Person, which includes every director and Band 1 executive, first obtains a written notice of 'no objection' from the Relevant Officer, who responds within about 48 hours, can refuse without reasons and can withdraw the notice before execution. Enforcement risk is unusually well handled: an involuntary disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is an Exempt Dealing provided the Policy was complied with when the facility was entered into, so a margin call or close-out in a Prohibited Period does not breach the Policy. The main constraints are timing (the Company Secretary may end a Trading Window without notice, and the no objection notice lapses at the end of the window), the short selling and stock lending bans, and mandatory disclosure of derivative and margin lending positions to Cochlear and potentially to the ASX.

PRU.title: Trading in Securities Policy
PRU.date_approved: 2024 (Rev. 2, approved by the Perseus Board; prepared by General Counsel & Company Secretary, reviewed by Chairman & CEO)

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: As defined in AASB 124, including the directors, the Company Secretary, the chief financial officer, those persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, and any other person notified by the Board. Bears all of the substantive restrictions: Prohibited Period ban, prior clearance, short-term trading and short selling bans, Board approval for encumbrances and margin loans, the derivatives criteria in section 10.4 and the notification rules.

tiers.name: Applicable Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, advisers and consultants of Perseus and its Group Companies. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, any additional restrictions imposed by the Board or executive management, and (if issued securities under a Perseus incentive plan) the section 10.3 hedging ban on unvested or holding-locked remuneration. Not otherwise subject to Prohibited Periods or clearance.

tiers.name: Related Persons
tiers.description: Applicable Persons' spouses, de facto spouses, parents and children, and entities controlled by Applicable Persons. Key Management Personnel's Related Persons are expressly bound by the Prohibited Period ban, the short-term trading and short selling bans and the clearance regime; for other Applicable Persons the policy only encourages counselling of Related Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Applicable Person to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested in that Applicable Person or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.start_anchor: two weeks before the release of the Company's quarterly report or half or full year financial statements to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: one Trading Day after that release

windows.start_anchor: commencement of any additional period imposed by Perseus's executive management or the Board when deemed necessary, notified in writing or by email
windows.end_anchor: end of the period stated in the notice, or until the restriction is revoked

PRU.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or Perseus's executive management may impose additional restrictions on Dealing by certain Applicable Persons involved in a potential project or transaction; such restrictions are part of the definition of Prohibited Period. They must be notified in writing or by email to affected Applicable Persons and run for the period stated in the notice or until revoked. The policy does not state that they are confidential, although refusal of clearance must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives over fully vested Perseus Securities are permitted only if all five criteria are met: the securities are fully vested; the Derivative matures outside any Prohibited Period known at inception; Perseus is not a counterparty; the Derivative is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options, or to protect the value of the security against tax liabilities; and the transaction complies with all applicable laws. The Dealing also needs section 7 clearance and post-trade notification with evidence that the criteria are satisfied.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving Derivatives in respect of Securities in Perseus if the following criteria are satisfied: The relevant Securities are fully vested; The Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside any Prohibited Period known at the time of entering into the transaction; Perseus is not a counterparty to the Derivative

rules.detail: The first criterion in section 10.4 is that the relevant Securities are fully vested, so any Derivative over unvested securities is outside the permission; section 10.2 separately applies the section 206J statutory ban on limiting exposure to unvested remuneration.
rules.evidence: The relevant Securities are fully vested

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock are treated the same as unvested remuneration; a Derivative limiting exposure to them contravenes section 206J of the Corporations Act, which the policy notes is an offence.
rules.evidence: must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Key Management Personnel to risk relating to an element of that Key Management Personnel's remuneration that has not vested in that Key Management Personnel or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Section 10.4 is confined to Key Management Personnel. For Applicable Persons who are not Key Management Personnel, the policy imposes no derivative criteria, clearance requirement or Prohibited Period restriction over fully vested unlocked securities; only the insider trading prohibition and any ad hoc additional restriction apply.

The section 206J statutory ban is imported for Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties, covering unvested remuneration and remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock. Contravention is a criminal offence.
rules.evidence: Pursuant to Section 206J of the Corporations Act, Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties (as that term is defined in the Corporations Act) must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Key Management Personnel to risk relating to an element of that Key Management Personnel's remuneration that has not vested

rules.detail: The policy extends the 206J-style ban beyond Key Management Personnel to any Applicable Person who has been issued securities under a Perseus incentive plan, such as options or performance rights, covering unvested awards and awards that have vested but remain holding-locked.
rules.evidence: any Applicable Person who has been issued with Securities under a Perseus incentive plan, such as options or performance rights, must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Applicable Person to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested in that Applicable Person or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging of fully vested, unlocked securities is permitted only through the section 10.4 gateway, which restricts the permitted purposes to protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options, or protecting the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities. A hedge for general portfolio diversification or liquidity does not qualify.
rules.evidence: The Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by Perseus or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but section 10.4 is a closed list: Key Management Personnel may 'only' use Derivatives for the two stated protective purposes. A derivative structure whose object is to raise cash against, or lock in the value of, a shareholding for general purposes fails the purpose criterion and is therefore not permitted.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving Derivatives in respect of Securities in Perseus if the following criteria are satisfied

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are prohibited from short selling Perseus Securities, defined as selling a security the seller does not own by borrowing it. No exemption route is provided for this ban.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons are prohibited from short selling Perseus's Securities.

rules.detail: Section 5.2 binds only Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons; the policy is silent on short selling by other Applicable Persons.

Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the Dealing definition, which covers only applying for, acquiring, disposing of, or agreeing to apply for, acquire or sell securities. It is referred to only descriptively in the definition of short selling.

CFDs are expressly named in the definition of Derivatives, so they are governed by the section 10.4 criteria: fully vested underlying, maturity outside a known Prohibited Period, Perseus not a counterparty, and one of the two permitted protective purposes. A short CFD would also engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Derivatives has the meaning given to that term in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes, without limitation, options and contracts for difference (CFDs)

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Perseus Securities are permitted with prior Board approval, which is also required for any changes to the arrangement. The terms must not require Dealings at a time when the Key Management Personnel is prohibited from Dealing, and the Key Management Personnel must keep the Company Secretary informed of changes relevant to continuous disclosure.
rules.evidence: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.

rules.detail: Granting any encumbrance over Perseus Securities requires prior Board approval, and further Board approval for any change to the arrangement. There is no outright ban and no distinction by vesting state, although securing unvested plan awards is not addressed.
rules.evidence: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.

rules.detail: Section 10.1 applies only to Key Management Personnel; the policy does not address encumbrances granted by other Applicable Persons.

The policy expressly contemplates 'a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities' and permits it with prior written Board approval. Section 10.4 also expressly contemplates a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options with the shares as the supporting asset. The lender's enforcement sale is an excluded Dealing only where prior written Board approval was obtained at entry.
rules.evidence: If Key Management Personnel or a Related Person enter into a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities, the relevant Key Management Personnel must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Perseus's continuous disclosure obligations.

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading, defined as the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period. The Board may exempt in exceptional circumstances on application, following the section 8.2 and 8.3 process.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading. The Board may on application, exempt a Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, with approval by the Managing Director; where the applicant is the Managing Director, by the Chairman; where the applicant is the Chairman, by the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee. Board approval instead for encumbrances and margin loans (10.1) and for Prohibited Period exemptions (8.1).
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (confirmation that the Dealing occurred and the price per Security); directors additionally provide Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z information for ASX filing
clearance.post_trade_deadline: Within two Trading Days of the Dealing; directors within three Trading Days of a change to their interest
clearance.evidence: Perseus's Key Management Personnel are required to obtain clearance for all intended Dealings in Perseus's Securities by themselves or, if they are aware, their Related Persons, at least two Trading Days before such intended Dealings. ... Any Dealing pursuant to this section must occur within 5 Trading Days of receipt of the Company Secretary's confirmation.
Obtain prior clearance for any intended transaction involving Perseus's Securities if the person is a member of Perseus's Key Management Personnel

short_term.basis: purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period
carve_outs: Board exemption on application in exceptional circumstances (sections 8.2 and 8.3 apply)
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading means the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period

exceptions.approver: Board
exceptions.evidence: The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only, give prior written clearance to any member of Perseus's Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons to sell, but not buy, Perseus's Securities during a Prohibited Period. ... Examples of exceptional circumstances include, but are not limited to: Severe Financial Hardship

exceptions.approver: Board
exceptions.evidence: Court orders requiring the sale of the Securities in question.

exceptions.approver: Board (prior written approval for entry into the arrangement)
exceptions.evidence: The disposing of Securities: ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement where prior written Board approval was received for entry into the arrangement under section 10.1(a) of the Policy
Entering into a transaction where the beneficial interest in Securities of Perseus will not change

exceptions.approver: prior written clearance in accordance with the Policy
exceptions.evidence: Under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

The issue of Securities in Perseus under: a rights issue; a dividend reinvestment plan; a share purchase plan; or an employee option plan, employee share acquisition scheme, executive share acquisition plan, performance rights plan or similar arrangement

The acceptance of (or undertaking to accept) an offer under a takeover bid, disposing of Securities under a scheme of arrangement or agreeing to cancel options or performance rights over unissued shares in conjunction with a change of control transaction
Exercising an option, exercising a right under an employee incentive scheme or converting a convertible security.
The transfer of Securities to a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Applicable Person or Related Person is a beneficiary

The investment in, or Dealing in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing only in Perseus's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require Dealings in Perseus's Securities at a time when they are prohibited from Dealing; no loan to value ratio or price trigger level is specified.
financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel: on entry into a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities, must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Perseus's continuous disclosure obligations; no fixed deadline
Key Management Personnel: Board approval required before granting encumbrances or entering margin loans, and again before any change to such arrangements (inception and variation)

Key Management Personnel: on use of Derivatives, notification to the Company Secretary under section 11 plus evidence that the section 10.4 criteria are satisfied, within two Trading Days of the Dealing
Directors: Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z information to the Company Secretary within three Trading Days of a change to the director's interest in Perseus's Securities, for filing with the ASX

external_documents: Perseus incentive plans (employee option plan, employee share acquisition scheme, executive share acquisition plan, performance rights plan)
Perseus disclosure policy (referred to in the definition of Inside Information)
PRU.exemption_authority: The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only, give prior written clearance for Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons to sell (but not buy) during a Prohibited Period, by Board resolution, written resolution or unanimous email consent; it may impose conditions and will not grant clearance if it considers the applicant holds Inside Information. The Board may also exempt from the short-term trading prohibition in exceptional circumstances. Any clearance may be refused at the Company's discretion without reasons and may be withdrawn if new information or a change of circumstances arises.
jurisdiction_overlays: TSX (Perseus is dual listed ASX/TSX; questions on compliance with ASX or TSX Listing Rules are directed to the Company Secretary)
Corporations Act section 206J statutory hedging prohibition, imported directly at section 10.2
Corporations Act section 205G and ASX Listing Rule 3.19A director notifications

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by Perseus or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a funded collar is permitted only where the loan funds the exercise price of Perseus options or the hedge protects against a tax liability, so a collar used to raise general liquidity against a vested holding fails the closed list of permitted purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside any Prohibited Period known at the time of entering into the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's expiry and any physical settlement date must be scheduled clear of the Closed Periods, which run from two weeks before to one Trading Day after each quarterly report and each half and full year result - roughly four blackouts a year - materially constraining tenor selection.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Perseus is not a counterparty to the Derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A third party bank counterparty is expressly required, which suits the proposed structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security over the collared shares needs full Board approval, not merely Company Secretary clearance, and every amendment, roll or top-up of the facility requires the Board to approve again.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale protection conditional on Board approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: The disposing of Securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement where prior written Board approval was received for entry into the arrangement under section 10.1(a) of the Policy [is excluded from the operation of this Policy].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is carved out of the Policy only if the Board approved the facility in writing at inception, so obtaining and documenting that approval is a condition precedent to any enforceable security.

bespoke_clauses.topic: loan terms must not force prohibited dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require Dealings in Perseus's Securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from Dealing in Perseus's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Margin call and close-out mechanics should be drafted so that the borrower is never obliged to trade during a Closed Period, for example by allowing cash cure, substitution of collateral or lender-side action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading means the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period. Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities are defined to include Derivatives and products that limit economic risk, entering and unwinding a collar inside three months could itself be Short-term Trading, so tenor should exceed three months absent a Board exemption.

bespoke_clauses.topic: securities definition sweeps in risk-limiting products
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include shares, debentures, renounceable or unrenounceable rights ... Derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are themselves Securities, so entry into and unwind of each leg is a Dealing requiring two Trading Days' prior clearance and post-trade notification within two Trading Days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance under this Policy may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. In such event the Company Secretary will notify the relevant Key Management Personnel who must withdraw any outstanding order for a Dealing in Perseus Securities promptly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is revocable up to execution, so pricing and signing should occur promptly within the five Trading Day window rather than in staged closings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition to the restrictions set out in section 10.2 of this Policy, any Applicable Person who has been issued with Securities under a Perseus incentive plan ... must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure ... to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested ... or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must confirm that every share in the collared parcel is both vested and free of any holding lock, and that no incentive plan participant below KMP level is hedging plan securities.

PRU.summary: A funded collar at Perseus is possible only in a narrow form. The secured loan leg is workable: section 10.1 permits Key Management Personnel to grant encumbrances and enter margin or other secured lending arrangements over Perseus Securities with prior written Board approval, and section 6.1(b) then excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the Policy altogether, provided that Board approval was obtained at entry. The derivative legs are the obstacle: section 10.4 permits Derivatives only where the securities are fully vested and free of any holding lock, Perseus is not a counterparty, the maturity falls outside any known Prohibited Period, and the Derivative is used either to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options or to protect against a tax liability. A collar entered to raise general liquidity against a vested holding does not meet that closed list of purposes and is therefore not permitted, while a collar over shares acquired on option exercise, protecting the asset supporting the exercise-price loan or an associated tax liability, fits squarely. Any such trade needs clearance two Trading Days in advance from the Company Secretary with Managing Director approval, must be executed within five Trading Days, must be notified within two Trading Days with evidence that the section 10.4 criteria are met, and should have a tenor beyond three months to avoid the Short-term Trading ban.

CDA.title: Share Trading Policy (Amended)
CDA.date_approved: Approved by the Board; reviewed regularly, no fixed cycle stated

tiers.name: designated officers
tiers.description: Directors, officers and executives of Codan Limited (and any family member or associate over whom they have influence). Only this tier must obtain prior written approval before dealing, under the section 11 protocol.

tiers.name: senior managers
tiers.description: Employees designated as senior managers and other employees who are likely to receive price-sensitive information in the course of their jobs. Bound by the blackout periods, the speculative dealing ban and the hedging ban, and must obtain prior approval before granting a lender rights over their Codan securities, but are not designated officers and so need no general pre-clearance to deal.

tiers.name: Codan employees
tiers.description: All employees of Codan Limited and its subsidiaries. Subject to the insider trading law and, under section 7, to the prohibition on hedging unvested options or performance rights and vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction.

tiers.name: closely-related parties
tiers.description: Immediate family members and associates (including companies and trusts) over whom the director, officer, executive or senior manager has influence. Expressly named alongside the principal in the blackout, speculative dealing, hedging, lender-rights approval and exceptional circumstances provisions.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions which would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance rights, or to a vested security which remains subject to a trading restriction

windows.start_anchor: 1 January
windows.end_anchor: close of trading on the next ASX trading day after the half-year results are released to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 1 July
windows.end_anchor: close of trading on the next ASX trading day after the full-year results are released to the ASX

CDA.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Codan Board may impose additional blackout periods from time to time. The fact that a blackout period is in place is to be treated as confidential information, although the Company's intranet provides daily information on whether or not a blackout period is in place.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule. Derivatives are within the definition of Securities, and Dealing covers acquiring them and making or offering to make an agreement with respect to acquiring or disposing of Securities or whose purpose is to secure a profit or gain in relation to the Securities. A designated officer therefore needs prior written approval under the section 11 protocol and cannot transact during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: "Securities" include shares of any class, notes, options, bonds, derivatives, ADRs, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Senior managers are bound by the blackout periods but are not designated officers, so no prior written approval is required for a derivative over vested unrestricted securities outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: the following persons are considered to be designated officers: Directors, officers and executives of Codan Limited (and any family member or associate over whom they have influence).

rules.detail: Any transaction, including a derivative, that limits exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance right is prohibited for all Codan employees and their closely-related parties.
rules.evidence: Codan employees and closely-related parties are prohibited from entering into transactions which would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance rights, or to a vested security which remains subject to a trading restriction.

rules.detail: The section 7 ban extends beyond unvested awards to any vested security that remains subject to a trading restriction, so shares released from performance conditions but still restricted cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: or to a vested security which remains subject to a trading restriction.

rules.detail: Express hedging prohibition covering unvested options and performance rights, applying to all Codan employees and their closely-related parties with no approval or exemption route.
rules.evidence: Codan employees and closely-related parties are prohibited from entering into transactions which would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance rights

rules.detail: The section 7 hedging ban is confined to unvested options and performance rights and to vested securities still subject to a trading restriction, so hedging a vested unrestricted holding is not prohibited. As a Dealing it requires prior written approval under section 11 and must occur outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into transactions which would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance rights, or to a vested security which remains subject to a trading restriction.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. The second limb of the Dealing definition catches any agreement whose purpose is to secure a profit or gain to a party in relation to the Securities, so a prepaid forward, collar or similar monetisation is a Dealing needing prior written approval, valid for five business days, outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: make or offer to make, or induce or attempt to induce a person to make or to offer to make, an agreement ... the purpose or purported purpose of which is to secure a profit or gain to a person who acquires, disposes of, subscribes for or underwrites the Securities or to any of the parties to the agreement in relation to the Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. The nearest provision is the section 6 ban on short-term or speculative trading, which is framed as an intention test at the time of purchase.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the Dealing definition, which is limited to acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for or underwriting Securities and agreements with respect to those acts or to securing a profit or gain.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives and so Securities; acquiring one is a Dealing requiring prior written approval for designated officers. A CFD would in practice contravene the section 6 ban on short-term or speculative trading.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Company directors, officers, executives, senior managers or closely-related parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly contemplated and permitted, subject to prior approval via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary before entering into the arrangement. A disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is then outside the Policy.
rules.evidence: where a disposal of securities of the Company occurs as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement (please note that prior approval must be obtained, via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, before entering into an agreement which provides a lender with rights over a director's, officer's, executive's, senior manager's or closely-related party's interests in the Company's securities)

rules.detail: Granting a lender rights over an interest in Codan securities is permitted with prior approval via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary. The requirement is drafted broadly as any agreement providing a lender with rights over securities interests, not only a margin loan, and extends to senior managers and closely-related parties.
rules.evidence: prior approval must be obtained, via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, before entering into an agreement which provides a lender with rights over a director's, officer's, executive's, senior manager's or closely-related party's interests in the Company's securities

rules.detail: The lender-rights approval requirement expressly names senior managers as well as directors, officers, executives and closely-related parties, so the approval gate applies even though senior managers need no general dealing approval.
rules.evidence: before entering into an agreement which provides a lender with rights over a director's, officer's, executive's, senior manager's or closely-related party's interests in the Company's securities

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing. Any agreement giving a lender rights over Codan securities requires prior approval via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, and once approved the lender's enforcement disposal falls outside the Policy, including during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: please note that prior approval must be obtained, via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, before entering into an agreement which provides a lender with rights over a director's ... interests in the Company's securities

rules.detail: The policy does not address whether unvested options, performance rights or restricted securities may be given as collateral; section 7 bans only transactions limiting exposure to risk on those holdings.

Directors, officers, executives, senior managers and closely-related parties must not engage in short-term or speculative trading. The guiding principle is an intention test: at the time of purchase the person should not intend to resell within 12 months with the aim of realising a capital gain. No carve-outs are stated and no approval route is offered.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Company directors, officers, executives, senior managers or closely-related parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities. Whilst it is impractical to provide a precise definition of what is short-term or speculative trading, the guiding principle should be that at the time of purchase the person should not intend to resell the securities within 12 months with the aim of realising a capital gain.

clearance.approver: For the Chairman: the Chairman of the Board Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee (or in his absence any other member of that Committee). For a Director or the Company Secretary: the Chairman of the Board (or in his absence the Chairman of the Board Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee). For an Executive: the Chief Executive Officer (or in his absence the Company Secretary). For an agreement giving a lender rights over securities: the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary.
clearance.post_trade_to: The Company (directors must notify the Company of any trading in the Company's securities, and notify the market of a substantial shareholding above five per cent or any change in it)

CDA.summary: A funded collar is feasible at Codan over fully vested shares that carry no trading restriction. The policy contains no ban on derivatives, monetisation or secured financing; the section 7 hedging prohibition bites only on unvested options and performance rights and on vested securities still subject to a trading restriction, so a collar over unrestricted vested shares is left to the general dealing regime. Two approvals are needed: the derivative and any associated dealing require prior written approval under the section 11 protocol (Board Chairman for directors, CEO for executives, Audit Risk & Compliance Committee Chairman for the Chairman), valid for five business days, and the security over the shares separately requires prior approval via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary before entering into any agreement giving a lender rights over the securities. Enforcement risk is well covered, because a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is expressly outside the Policy, so a close-out during a blackout does not breach it. The principal constraints are the blackout periods from 1 January and 1 July until the day after the half and full year results plus any confidential Board-imposed blackout, and the unusually long section 6 speculative dealing rule, which suggests a tenor of more than twelve months and no early-realisation intent.

AFI.exemption_authority: Only a narrow exceptional circumstances discretion: a KMP not in possession of inside information may be given written clearance to sell (but not purchase) securities when otherwise prohibited, where they are in severe financial difficulty or another exceptional circumstance such as a court order applies. Requests go to the Chairman (or MD) for Directors and to the MD (or Chairman) for Senior Executives, must be accompanied by particulars, and no KMP may approve their own transaction. The Company may be required to notify the existence of exceptional circumstances to the ASX. There is no authority to waive the section 2.5 secured financing ban or the section 2.6 hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: the loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every Non-Executive Director and Senior Executive with no approval route and no vesting carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.topic: conflict from loans over other securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must also use their best endeavours to ensure they are not put in a position of conflict with this policy by virtue of having margin or other loans over other securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a facility secured on a different portfolio must not create a position that could force dealings in AFIC securities, so cross-collateralised or portfolio-wide lending is also constrained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The section 3 exclusions list contains no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, in contrast to most ASX trading policies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consistent with the outright ban on pledging, there is no mechanism by which a lender's enforcement sale during a prohibited period would fall outside the policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested executive equity
bespoke_clauses.clause: Senior Executives are prohibited from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities they may receive as part of their performance-based remuneration (hedging). Breaches of the Company's policy in this regard will normally result in the termination of the Senior Executive's employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is narrow, covering only unvested performance equity of Senior Executives, so unfunded put and call legs over vested shares are not themselves prohibited, but the penalty for getting the vesting analysis wrong is dismissal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy defines neither 'deal' nor 'securities' and contains no derivatives, encumbrance or agreement-to-deal limbs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Whether an OTC option over AFIC shares is a 'dealing' requiring prior notice is left open, so the bank should assume the notification requirements apply and seek confirmation from the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman (or in his absence the MD) and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside a prohibited period the regime is prior notification rather than approval, so if the secured financing ban did not apply the option legs would need only notice and immediate post-trade advice to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A KMP ... may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited by this policy from doing so if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only relief available is for an outright sale in a prohibited period; it cannot be used to authorise a pledge, a derivative or a purchase leg such as buying a put.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities during ... the duration of the pricing period for any capital management event.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a listed investment company, capital management events such as placements, buy-backs and share purchase plans create unscheduled blackouts on top of the December and June periods, restricting when any structure could be entered, reset or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP may be required annually and from time to time to verify in writing (including by email) that they have complied with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A KMP with a secured facility over AFIC shares would have to disclose the breach on their annual certification, making the arrangement impossible to maintain quietly.

AFI.summary: A funded collar is not possible for AFIC Key Management Personnel. Section 2.5 prohibits KMP from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans, which bars the secured loan leg outright; the ban is drafted to catch any loan, applies to Non-Executive Directors and Senior Executives alike and to their Closely Connected Persons and Entities, and there is no approval, waiver or exceptional circumstances route to relax it. The derivative legs are less constrained: the section 2.6 hedging prohibition reaches only unvested performance-based remuneration securities of Senior Executives, so a put and call over vested unrestricted shares is not expressly prohibited, and outside prohibited periods a KMP need only give prior notice to the Chairman or MD and the CFO or Company Secretary and advise the Company Secretary immediately after the transaction. Any such structure would still have to avoid the December and June prohibited periods and any capital management pricing period, avoid short selling, and be consistent with the requirement that dealings be for investment and not trading purposes. In practice an unfunded collar could be structured but the funding secured on the collared shares cannot, so the bank would need to lend on an unsecured basis or against other collateral entirely.

rules.detail: Hedging with financial products, which covers OTC puts and calls, is expressly permitted over vested and unrestricted Company securities. The hedge transaction is treated as a dealing, so a director or the CEO must obtain prior written approval from the Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair, from the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee) and must not transact during a blackout period. The blackout ban expressly extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Hedging vested and unrestricted Company securities is expressly permitted provided the transaction is treated as a dealing and the paragraph 4.1 approval or paragraph 4.2 notification requirements are satisfied. rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar or similar structure over vested unrestricted shares is a dealing (it is a financial product issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities and an agreement to sell securities) and would generally also be a hedge under paragraph 4.4, so it needs paragraph 4.1 approval or 4.2 notification. Forward contracts are given as an example of short-term dealings, so a short-dated monetisation is caught by paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is not named in this Policy. Relevant Persons are also subject to the Company's separate Insider Trading Policy, which is not part of this document.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the description of dealing, which extends to exercising options and to procuring and entering into agreements to subscribe for, buy or sell securities.

CFDs are not named but are transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities, so they fall within the definition of hedging and are permitted over vested unrestricted holdings subject to approval or notification. An actively traded CFD position would breach the short-term trading ban in paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted. Entering into the arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account and selling securities to satisfy a margin call are each dealings. Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain paragraph 4.1 approval for any such dealing irrespective of any trading window, and the Company may impose conditions on that approval.
rules.evidence: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.

rules.detail: Senior executives, who otherwise only notify after dealing, are pulled up into the director-level prior approval regime for any dealing connected with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
rules.evidence: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.

rules.detail: Granting security is not prohibited. The only express encumbrance regime is for margin lending arrangements, where entry and the transfer of securities into the loan account are dealings requiring approval. A pledge outside a margin lending arrangement is not separately named, although paragraph 4.5(g) contemplates secured lenders generally.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in the Company's securities by Relevant Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must be conducted in accordance with this Policy. Such dealings will include: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing. The Policy regulates margin lending expressly and, subject to paragraph 4.3, excludes from the approval and blackout rules a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights. The Company may make any margin lending approval conditional, for example on the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: subject to paragraph 4.3, a disposal of securities of the Company or the securities of Yanzhou that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: The Policy does not address whether unvested equity plan holdings or securities under a holding lock may be given as collateral; paragraph 4.4 restricts only hedging of those holdings.

Relevant Persons must not deal on a short-term trading basis, which includes buying and selling on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as the example. No carve-outs are listed and no waiver is provided, although the paragraph 4.5 exclusions disapply paragraphs 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.4 but not paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

For a waiver to deal during a blackout period: the Chair or Vice-Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee (for the Chair or Vice-Chair), or their delegate.

The Relevant Person must undertake the proposed dealing as soon as possible once the notification is provided or approval is granted or such other period specified in the approval.

short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

The application must be in writing with sufficient evidence that the dealing is the only reasonable course of action, and any waiver granted lasts 1 business day. There is no authority to waive the paragraph 4.4(b) hedging prohibitions or the paragraph 3.3 short-term trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: express permission to hedge vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications are made on this basis; and the relevant requirements under paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of this Policy have been satisfied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an express, affirmative permission for the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares, subject only to the ordinary approval and notification machinery - among the clearest hedging permissions on the ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the hedge transaction must not be entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Relevant Person is in possession of inside information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every roll, reset, amendment and unwind of the collar is separately gated, so the documentation must not require the executive to act at a fixed date that could coincide with possession of inside information.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending approval overrides trading windows
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg is required at all times, but the phrase 'irrespective of any trading window' also signals that such approval can be sought and given outside an open window, which helps if the facility must be varied during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with 4.3(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement terms of the bank's facility, for example restricting when collateral may be sold on a margin call, so the credit terms must be agreed with the issuer as well as the borrower.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to paragraph 4.3, a disposal of securities of the Company or the securities of Yanzhou that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from paragraphs 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.4].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement, including during a blackout, is carved out of the blackout and approval rules provided the paragraph 4.3 approval regime was observed, so the bank's security can be enforced without putting the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: borrower-side margin call sales are dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Such dealings will include: ... selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A sale by the executive to meet a margin call is a dealing needing prior approval, so the facility should rely on lender-exercised rights or cash cure rather than obliging the borrower to sell.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts means a short-dated collar or forward-settled leg risks characterisation as prohibited short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed three months and the exclusions in paragraph 4.5 do not disapply this ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The existence and nature of the collar may be publicly disclosed, so the parties should assume no confidentiality over the structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a waiver is granted, the Relevant Person will be notified in writing (which may include notification via email) and in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 1 business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any blackout waiver gives only a single business day to price and execute, which is impractical for negotiating a collar, so the transaction must be planned for an open period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: four blackouts a year plus Yanzhou securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons must not deal in the securities of the Company or Yanzhou Coal Mining Company Limited (Yanzhou) during any of the following blackout periods [31 December, 30 June, 31 March and 30 September, each until the day after the relevant results or quarterly report].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly blackouts leave relatively short open periods for entry and unwind, and the same restrictions apply to dealings in the listed parent's securities, which matters if the hedge references Yanzhou rather than Yancoal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Relevant Person must undertake the proposed dealing as soon as possible once the notification is provided or approval is granted or such other period specified in the approval. If the dealing is not undertaken within this time, the notification will no longer have effect and new notification or approval will be required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no fixed validity period, only an 'as soon as possible' standard, so the approval should specify an express window long enough to document and settle the collar and the loan.

YAL.summary: A funded collar is workable at Yancoal over vested and unrestricted shares. Paragraph 4.4(c) expressly permits Relevant Persons to hedge vested and unrestricted Company securities, defining hedging as transactions in financial products that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities, provided the hedge is treated as a dealing and cleared under the ordinary machinery: prior written approval from the Chair of the Board for directors, the CEO and the CEC, and post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for everyone else. The financing leg is also available: paragraph 4.3 regulates rather than bans margin lending, requiring directors and senior executives to obtain paragraph 4.1 approval for entering the arrangement, transferring shares into the loan account or selling to meet a call, irrespective of any trading window, and the Company may attach conditions including on when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call; a lender's enforcement disposal is then excluded from the blackout and approval rules. The hard limits are that securities must never be hedged before vesting or while subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction, that no hedge may be entered, renewed, altered or closed out while the person holds inside information, and that the tenor must exceed three months because paragraph 3.3 treats forward contracts as prohibited short-term dealings. Practical constraints are the four annual blackout periods around the full year, half year and two quarterly reports plus any Board-specified period, the one business day duration of any exceptional circumstances waiver, and the Company's right to disclose the fact and nature of the hedge in its annual report or to the ASX.

GGP.title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Greatland Personnel
tiers.description: All full-time, part-time and casual employees, contractors, consultants and advisers of Greatland Resources Limited and Group companies, as well as all Restricted Persons. Bound by the general prohibition (1.2, 2.1) and by the bans on short-term trading, short selling and hedging (2.2), but not by the Trading Window / Dealing Approval regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers, KMPs, PDMRs and the Company Secretary of Greatland and Group companies, plus other Group employees designated by the Managing Director and Company Secretary, and persons associated with them (close family; entities, trusts or investment vehicles they control, materially influence or benefit from; business and other associates). Prohibited from Dealing at all unless permitted by the remainder of the Policy.

tiers.name: Directors, PDMRs, Company Secretary
tiers.description: Directors, PDMRs (senior officers with regular access to inside information and power to take managerial decisions) and the Company Secretary, and persons associated with them. They have no general declared Trading Window: their Trading Window is only the period in which a Dealing Approval applies, and approval comes from the Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director).

tiers.name: Other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are not Directors, PDMRs or the Company Secretary. They may Deal without a specific Dealing Approval during a Trading Window declared by the Chair; outside a Trading Window they need a Dealing Approval from the Managing Director (direct reports) or otherwise the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Persons discharging managerial responsibilities for MAR/AIM purposes: a Director, or a senior officer who is not a Director but has regular access to inside information and power to take managerial decisions affecting the Company's future development. Subject to the additional MAR Closed Periods, the exceptional-circumstances-only approval gate, and FCA/RNS notification.

tiers.name: persons closely associated (PCA)
tiers.description: A PDMR's spouse or civil partner; a child or step-child under 18 who is unmarried and has no civil partner; a relative sharing the household for at least a year; and a legal person, trust or partnership managed by, controlled by, set up for the benefit of, or whose economic interests are substantially equivalent to those of, such a person. They must not Deal except during a Trading Window and must notify the Company Secretary immediately.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into an arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: publication of the Company's half-yearly results

windows.end_anchor: declaration of a Trading Window or grant of a Dealing Approval

windows.end_anchor: the information ceases to be withheld

GGP.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director) may at any time, by written notification to relevant Restricted Persons, close a declared Trading Window, and may shorten the Validity Period of any Dealing Approval by written notice. Separately, under 2.1 Greatland may give notice to any or all Greatland Personnel that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until further notice. Prohibited Periods arise automatically and confidentially whenever the Company is withholding disclosable information under ASX LR 3.1A, MAR art 17(4) or the AIM Rule 11 guidance notes.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule. 'Securities' expressly includes derivative instruments, other linked financial instruments and 'instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held', with no venue limitation, so an OTC put or call over Greatland shares is a Security; entering into, amending or terminating any agreement (even conditional) in respect of Securities is a Dealing. Restricted Persons are therefore prohibited from writing or buying such an option except under a Dealing Approval (or, for Other Restricted Persons, within a declared Trading Window). Note the put leg may separately offend the position-based short-selling ban in 2.2(b).
rules.evidence: Securities means shares, options, share rights ... and any other equity, debt or derivative instruments, or other linked financial instruments, including instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held.

rules.detail: For personnel who are not Restricted Persons there is no clearance route, only the flat bans. A derivative that limits the exposure of unvested or holding-locked remuneration is a prohibited hedge, and any derivative position that would profit from a decline in the share price is prohibited short selling. Derivatives outside those two descriptions are not addressed for this tier.
rules.evidence: Greatland Personnel must not engage in: ... Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any arrangement having the effect of limiting exposure to risk relating to unvested remuneration. The Policy also notes that the Corporations Act independently prohibits such hedging by KMP (including Directors) and their closely related parties.
rules.evidence: Hedging transactions of Company Securities, meaning entering into an arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The hedging ban expressly extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock, so a collar over shares still inside a disposal restriction period is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The express hedging ban is confined to unvested or holding-locked remuneration, so hedging fully vested and unrestricted shares is not itself prohibited. It remains a Dealing (an instrument to limit the economic risk of securities held is a Security) requiring a prior written Dealing Approval and, for non-PDMR Restricted Persons, a declared Trading Window. The put leg must still be tested against the short-selling ban in 2.2(b).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are also prohibited from Dealing in Company Securities unless permitted by the remainder of this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and equity swaps are not named. Each is caught as a Dealing: entering into a conditional agreement to sell Securities, and, under 8(a)(ii), any contractual arrangement by which the person may become contractually obliged to a third party to Deal. Prior Dealing Approval is required, and 8(c) says such approval should not be expected where the arrangement carries the risk of a forced trade in a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: otherwise transact, including (without limitation) using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation and entering into, amending or terminating any agreement (even if it is conditional) to subscribe for, buy or sell, or exercise or convert, any Securities

rules.detail: Flat prohibition applying to all Personnel including Restricted Persons, with no approval route. The definition is drafted by economic effect and by 'position', not by settlement or borrowing, so it is wide enough to capture a purchased put or any downside-profiting leg of a collar even where the shares are held outright.
rules.evidence: Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).

rules.detail: Share loans are named only in the heading of Section 8; the operative text catches them as a contractual arrangement under which an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to the person's Company Securities is assigned to or exercisable by another party. Such Dealing is not permitted other than with a Dealing Approval, and 8(c) discourages approval.
rules.evidence: Dealing in Company Securities includes the grant of a security interest over Company Securities and any other contractual arrangement where: an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to Company Securities of a Restricted Person is assigned to or is exercisable by another party

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative or linked financial instrument and so a Security, but a short CFD is a position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities and is therefore prohibited outright; a long CFD would be a Dealing requiring a Dealing Approval.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities

rules.detail: Margin loans and margin calls are named in the Section 8 heading and margin call arrangements are expressly listed as arrangements under which the person may become contractually obliged to Deal. They are not banned outright, but are a Dealing requiring a Dealing Approval, and 8(c) warns that approval should not be expected because of the risk of a forced trade during a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person may become contractually obliged to a third party to Deal in Company Securities, including but not limited to margin call arrangements.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Company Securities is expressly a Dealing, both under the general definition (using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation) and under Section 8(a). It is not permitted other than with a Dealing Approval; the same Dealing must be notified to the Company Secretary within two Business Days and, for Directors, announced to ASX.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this Policy, Dealing in Company Securities includes the grant of a security interest over Company Securities

rules.detail: Using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation is a Dealing and is permitted only with a Dealing Approval. There is no outright ban, but 8(c) sets a strong presumption against approval for any arrangement carrying forced-trade risk, which is exactly the profile of a loan secured on collared shares with lender enforcement rights.
rules.evidence: A Dealing Approval under (b) should not be expected to be given to a Restricted Person having regard to the risk of a forced trade in Company Securities as part of the arrangement during a Prohibited Period, and the consequential legal and market reputational risk.

rules.detail: Section 8 is expressed to apply to Restricted Persons only; the Policy says nothing about secured financing by personnel who are not Restricted Persons, beyond the general requirement to Deal only in compliance with the Policy.

Short term buying and selling is prohibited for all Personnel, with selling within three months of buying given as guidance rather than a bright line. Restricted Persons seeking approval to sell must disclose when they last bought if relevant.
rules.evidence: Short term buying and selling of Company Securities. In considering what is “short term” for the purposes of this Policy, selling within three (3) months of buying securities in the Company is given as guidance.

clearance.approver: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director). The Chair must obtain approval from the Deputy Chair, or from the Managing Director and one non-executive Director jointly. No one may approve their own or an associate's Dealing.

clearance.evidence: Any Director, PDMR (as defined in Section 3.1(p) below) or Company Secretary, or any persons associated with them, must obtain Dealing Approval from the Chair (or in their absence by the Deputy Chair or Managing Director). ... A Dealing Approval is valid for two Business Days (excluding the day that the approval is received)

clearance.approver: The Managing Director for direct reports of the Managing Director; otherwise the Company Secretary (either may consult the Chair). No Dealing Approval is needed for Dealing during a Trading Window declared by the Chair.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Business Days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: During Trading Windows, Dealing in Company Securities by Restricted Persons (other than a Director, Company Secretary or other PDMR) is permitted, without a specific Dealing Approval.

clearance.approver: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director); during a MAR Closed Period or Prohibited Period approval will only be granted in exceptional circumstances

clearance.post_trade_deadline: Company Secretary within two working days of the trade; FCA no later than three working days after the trade
clearance.evidence: During MAR Closed Periods, Dealing in Company Securities by PDMRs is prohibited other than pursuant to a Dealing Approval, which will only be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as those set out in Section 5(c) below.

In addition to the above prohibitions applicable to all Greatland Personnel, Restricted Persons are also prohibited from Dealing in Company Securities unless permitted by the remainder of this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (The Corporations Act also prohibits such hedging transactions for persons who have authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity (including Directors) and their closely related parties.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For KMP and their closely related parties the ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked remuneration is statutory as well as contractual, so no company approval could cure a collar over that portion of the holding.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Reputational perception is an independent breach standard, and Section 5(a)(iii) makes 'adverse reputational imputations' a stated ground for refusing approval, which is a live risk for a publicly disclosable director collar.
