bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved collar becomes a matter of Board record as well as market disclosure, so the transaction cannot be kept confidential within the company.

GGP.summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted shares is theoretically available to a Restricted Person but only on tight conditions and with real legal risk. Every element - the OTC put and call (Securities in their own right, expressly including 'instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held'), the grant of a security interest, and any arrangement that could oblige the executive to Deal - is a Dealing requiring prior written Dealing Approval from the Chair (Managing Director or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons), valid only two Business Days and revocable, with notification to the Company Secretary within two Business Days and ASX Appendix 3Y, FCA and RNS disclosure for Directors and PDMRs. Two provisions are close to fatal: Section 8(c) says a Dealing Approval for a secured or forced-trade-risk arrangement 'should not be expected to be given', and Section 2.2(b) bans, for all Personnel with no approval route, any 'transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price' of the shares, which on its face reaches the purchased put. Any shares that are unvested or vested but subject to a holding lock cannot be collared at all, that ban being both contractual and statutory for KMP. As a dual ASX/AIM issuer the company also imposes MAR Closed Periods from 1 July and 31 December until the respective results, during which a PDMR can only deal in exceptional circumstances, and for Directors and PDMRs there is no standing open window at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to hedging, limiting economic risk, short selling, securities lending, margin calls or forced sales.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly-reporting miner the Company is closed for the whole gap between each quarter end and its quarterly report, on top of the four-week pre-results windows, leaving only short and irregular execution windows for pricing a collar.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The OTC put and call are within the Policy's scope even though no clause addresses derivatives, so both legs are subject to the Closed Period and pre-approval regime but to no substantive prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Restricted Person must satisfy the Chairman that the circumstances are exceptional and that the proposed sale or disposal of the securities is the only reasonable course of action available to them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy does not address margin calls, forced sales by a financier, or sales by a third party outside the executive's control.

CMM.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive. Nothing in it prohibits hedging, short selling, securities lending or derivatives; derivatives and financial products created over or in respect of Capricorn securities are simply brought within the Policy's scope, so both collar legs are treated as ordinary dealings. The single hard constraint on the loan leg is 5.13: a Director or Key Management Person may not enter into a funding arrangement over their Capricorn shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares, so the collared parcel must be sized below that threshold against issued capital. Execution must be pre-approved by the Chairman or Company Secretary before any purchase or sale, must fall outside the Closed Periods (four weeks before the half and full year results, the whole period from each quarter end until two business days after the Quarterly Report, and 30 days before a disclosure document) and outside any discretionary restricted trading period, with a Trading Notification form to the Company Secretary within 2 days and ASX notification of a Director's change in relevant interest within 5 business days. The Policy is silent on margin calls and forced sales, so the bank's enforcement and settlement rights during a closed period should be agreed with the Chairman in advance.

TPG.exemption_authority: The relevant designated officer (the Chairperson for Directors, the Chairperson of the Audit Committee for the Chairperson, the Chief Executive Officer for Senior Executives) may give written acknowledgement permitting a trade outside a Window Period, typically in Exceptional Circumstances. The acknowledgement is expressly a compliance monitoring function only and not an endorsement of the transaction, and the individual remains responsible for compliance with the law.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants of TPG Telecom may take out margin loans over their vested holdings in TPG Telecom's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted rather than banned, provided it is secured only over vested holdings; this is one of the few ASX policies that affirmatively allows a director to encumber shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: However, Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants must not allow a margin call to be met by the sale of TPG Telecom's Securities at a time when they would not be able to sell those Securities themselves under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement and physical settlement rights must be drafted so that no sale of the collared shares can occur outside a Window Period or during an ad hoc closed period without the executive first obtaining written acknowledgement, otherwise the executive breaches the Policy through the lender's own action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The details of the Security Arrangements which must be provided must include the number of Securities of TPG Telecom involved, any trigger points, the right of the lender or security holder to sell the Securities unilaterally and any other material details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Commercial terms of the facility, including margin triggers and the bank's unilateral sale rights, must be handed to the Chairperson or CEO at inception and on every non-trivial amendment, and may be announced to the market under Listing Rule 3.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written acknowledgement is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction. Individuals remain responsible for their compliance with the law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot treat the designated officer's acknowledgement as company sign-off on the collar's legality, so it should obtain its own confirmation on insider information and plan-rule compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives are only permitted to deal in TPG Telecom's Securities during a one month period following the release of TPG Telecom's half yearly and annual results ... and TPG Telecom's Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a closed-by-default policy with only three one-month windows a year, so collar entry, roll and unwind must be scheduled into those windows or justified as Exceptional Circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Outside the Window Period, Directors and Senior Executives may in certain circumstances (for example, Exceptional Circumstances) trade in TPG Telecom's Securities following written acknowledgement in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The annexed form requires details of the Exceptional Circumstances, so a voluntary financing transaction is unlikely to be executable outside a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include shares of any class, options, bonds, derivatives, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Derivatives are listed expressly, but the closing words 'able to be traded on a financial market' could be argued to confine the definition to exchange-traded products, leaving it unclear whether a bilateral OTC put and call are Securities for Policy purposes; confirm the company's view before relying on either reading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives must not deal in TPG Telecom's Securities for short term gain. Short term means a period of three months or less.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind should exceed three months, and the structure should not be characterised as dealing for short term gain.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no hedging prohibition, no restriction on hedging unvested or holding-locked equity, and no short-selling prohibition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is prohibited by the trading policy itself; the constraints on hedging unvested incentive securities would have to come from the plan rules and section 206J of the Corporations Act, which are outside this document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it may lead to disciplinary action being taken against the person, including disposal of any TPG Telecom Securities acquired in breach of this Policy and/or dismissal in serious cases.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can trigger forced disposal of the underlying shares, which would cut across a collar and the bank's security position.

TPG.summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at TPG Telecom, which is among the most permissive ASX policies on financing. The Policy expressly allows Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants to take out margin loans over their vested holdings and contemplates that they may 'otherwise encumber' their Securities, subject only to disclosure of the Security Arrangements to the designated officer (the Chairperson for Directors, the CEO for Senior Executives) on entry and on any non-trivial change, including the number of shares, trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale rights, which may in turn be disclosed to ASX under Listing Rule 3.1. There is no hedging, short-selling or derivatives prohibition, and derivatives fall within the definition of Securities, so both option legs are ordinary dealings that must be executed inside one of the three one-month Window Periods following the half year results, the annual results and the AGM, or outside them with written acknowledgement supported by Exceptional Circumstances. The critical structuring constraint is that a margin call must not be met by a sale of TPG Telecom Securities at a time when the executive could not sell, so the bank's enforcement and physical-settlement rights must be conditioned on Policy-permitted timing. Collateral should be limited to vested holdings and the tenor should exceed three months to stay clear of the short-term gain prohibition.

The Board may also amend the Policy and extend or shorten a permitted period at any time, with notice by email or other written means. The Policy says nothing about whether the reason for a prohibition is confidential.

rules.section: The Company's Trading Policy (b) Specific Prohibition
rules.detail: A flat ban, with no approval route and no venue distinction, on using derivatives in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities. It is expressed together with hedging arrangements and applies to all directors, officers, employees and regular consultants.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities.

rules.section: Insider Trading (definition of the Company's Securities); (b); (d)
rules.detail: The express derivatives ban reaches only unvested Securities. For vested Securities a derivative is caught by the definition of the Company's Securities, which expressly includes any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties, with no venue limitation on that limb. Dealing therefore requires a completed Trade Notification Form with Part B signed by the Chairman (or the Managing Director for the Chairman), must fall outside the blackout periods, and must be confirmed to the Company Secretary afterwards.
rules.evidence: The Company's Securities means shares, options or other financial products issued by Ramelius that are traded on the Australian Securities Exchange Limited (“ASX”) and include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities are prohibited outright. Hedging is not defined, so the scope of what constitutes a hedging arrangement is left open, and there is no discretion to permit it.
rules.evidence: must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities

rules.detail: The prohibition is keyed to Securities being unvested. The Policy says nothing about Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or disposal restriction, so such shares are not caught by the express ban, though the plan rules (not incorporated) may restrict them.

Hedging vested Ramelius Securities is not prohibited. The hedging instrument is itself a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities and so a Security, meaning the prior notification, blackout and trade confirmation requirements apply but no substantive prohibition does.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must not deal in Ramelius Securities without first completing Part A of a Notification to Trade in Ramelius Securities Form

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. Each involves a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities and an agreement to dispose of Securities, both of which are caught, so prior notification and Chairman sign-off are required and the transaction cannot be entered into during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: trade or deal in (i.e. apply for, acquire or dispose) the Company's Securities or enter into an agreement to trade in the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and there is no economic-effect or downside-position test.
Securities lending is not mentioned and the trading definitions cover only applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and agreements to do so.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Ramelius shares is a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities by a third party and so falls within the Policy, requiring prior notification and Chairman sign-off; over unvested Securities it would be a prohibited derivative.
rules.evidence: include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties

rules.detail: Margin lending, margin calls and forced sales by a financier are not mentioned anywhere in this 2011 policy. There is no prohibition, no approval requirement and no disclosure obligation attaching to a margin loan as such.

Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Ramelius Securities is not addressed. The trading definitions extend only to applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and to agreements to do so, so the grant of security is not on its face a trade requiring notification, although the eventual enforcement sale would be a disposal.

There is no secured financing clause of any kind: no prohibition, no threshold, no disclosure of financing arrangements, no LVR or trigger guidance, and no treatment of a lender's unilateral sale rights.
The Policy contains no short-term or speculative trading restriction, no minimum holding period and no intention test.

RMS.exemption_authority: The Chairman, or the Managing Director in the case of the Chairman, may exercise a discretion to allow a trade outside a permitted period where the person declares exceptional circumstances (such as a pressing financial commitment or hardship) and that they hold no inside information, via a Trade Notification Form. The discretion may only be exercised before the trade and not after the event, and the trade remains subject to paragraphs (a), (b) and (d) to (f), so it cannot cure the ban on derivatives and hedging over unvested Securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only substantive obstacle to a collar: it bites only on unvested Securities, so a collar over fully vested shares is not prohibited, but the collared parcel must be strictly segregated from any unvested performance rights or options.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notification is not approval but carries a veto
bespoke_clauses.clause: Notification of any trade and completion of Part B of a Trade Notification Form does not constitute approval by or on behalf of Ramelius for the relevant trade. ... the Chairman ... must ... either complete Part B ... or direct the director/officer/employee that the trade should not be undertaken. A director/officer/employee must comply with the direction given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank gets no company approval it can rely on, but the Chairman holds an unqualified veto with no criteria, no response deadline and no stated validity period for a completed Part B, so timing risk on pricing the collar sits with the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, security interests, encumbrances, forced sales, short selling, securities lending or short-term trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is unregulated by this policy, but that silence cuts both ways: there is no framework permitting or disclosing the financing and no protection against the bank's enforcement sale falling in a blackout period, so the position should be documented with the Chairman up front.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company's Securities ... include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put and call over Ramelius shares are the Company's Securities for Policy purposes, so entering into, and later unwinding, each leg is a trade needing a Trade Notification Form and Chairman sign-off outside a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.topic: frequent blackouts for a quarterly reporter
bespoke_clauses.clause: during the period between the end of the Company's full financial year and the announcement of the Company's full year financial results ... during the period between the end of the Company's half year and the announcement of the Company's half year financial results ... during the one week period immediately prior to the lodgement of the Company's quarterly activity reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The full-year and half-year blackouts run from period end to results announcement, which can be six to eight weeks each, and every quarterly report adds a further week, materially narrowing the dates on which a collar can be struck or rolled.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Board of Directors may determine that there are specific periods when directors, officers and employees are permitted to deal ... The Board of Directors may from time to time amend this trading policy or may extend or shorten a permitted period for dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Dealing windows are defined by Board determination rather than by fixed anchors and can be shortened at will, so a scheduled roll or unwind of the collar can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The discretion may only be exercised before a trade in the Company's Securities and not after the event.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security or the collar physically settles during a prohibited period, the breach cannot be cured retrospectively, so settlement mechanics must be conditioned on prior notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers, employees (including regular consultants) must take reasonable steps to prohibit dealing in the Company's Securities by immediate family and companies, trusts or other entities over which the director, officer, employee and regular consultant or immediate family member has control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the Policy, and the obligation is framed as taking reasonable steps to prohibit their dealing altogether.

RMS.summary: A funded collar over fully vested Ramelius shares is possible under this policy, which is short, dated December 2011, and silent on financing. The only substantive prohibition relevant to the structure is that derivatives and hedging arrangements must not be used in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities, so the collared parcel must consist solely of vested shares. Both option legs are nevertheless the Company's Securities, because the definition expressly includes any financial or associated product issued or created over those Securities by third parties, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trade Notification Form with Part B signed by the Chairman (the Managing Director for the Chairman) and a Trade Confirmation Form to the Company Secretary, and must avoid the blackout from each period end to the results announcement, the week before each quarterly activity report, and any Board-determined prohibition. Part B is expressly not an approval, yet the Chairman can direct that a trade not be undertaken, so the bank obtains no reliance from the process. Margin lending, security interests, forced sales and short selling are entirely unaddressed, meaning the loan leg is not prohibited but also carries no agreed treatment for enforcement during a blackout, and the discretion to permit an out-of-window trade cannot be exercised after the event.

JBH.title: JB Hi-Fi Limited - Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee of any JB Hi-Fi Group company, including each Key Person. Only Sections 1 and 2 (the insider trading prohibition) apply to Employees who are not Key Persons; the trading windows, approval, hedging and margin lending rules in Section 3 do not.

tiers.name: Key Persons
tiers.description: KMP of the JB Hi-Fi Group within AASB 124 plus certain other key employees: any Director, the Group Executive team, the Executive teams of the JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys and E&S businesses, members of the senior management teams, area and territory managers, Support Office employees in Australia and New Zealand, store managers, store office administrators and administrators, and anyone else designated by the Company Secretary. All Sections of the Policy apply to Key Persons: trading windows, the 6 month rule and the unvested hedging ban. Only the sub-group listed in section 3.8 (Directors, Group and business Executive teams, Company Secretary, direct reports of the Group CFO, the legal team and any person designated by the Company Secretary) needs prior written approval to Deal inside a Trading Window.

rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities

rules.evidence: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant

rules.evidence: Once any equity-based incentive award or grant made by JB Hi-Fi to a Key Person (who is not a Director or Executive) is vested and is exercisable, the restriction in section 3.30 above does not apply.

rules.detail: Not named for Key Persons generally. bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives includes derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars) and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is expressly within scope, so both legs are Dealings and the substance test catches any economically equivalent structure, but nothing prohibits a collar over vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities (whether received under an equity-based incentive award scheme or otherwise).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar is available to Directors and Executives over vested and on-market shares but only on a wholly discretionary approval that may be refused without reasons and revoked before execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: voluntary public disclosure of hedges and loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: JB Hi-Fi may publicly disclose this information irrespective of whether it is technically required by law or the ASX Listing Rules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the collar and the secured loan may be announced to the market even where no legal disclosure obligation exists, so the client cannot rely on confidentiality.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement ... without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to approval and disclosure rather than prohibited, so a funded structure is achievable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval given under section 3.22 by the Relevant Company Officer will be valid for a period of 5 trading days, commencing on the date it is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both the collar and the loan must complete within 5 trading days of each approval or fresh approval is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval given may be revoked in writing (including by email) by the Relevant Company Officer prior to Dealing taking place if new information comes to light, or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank faces execution risk that a signed but unsettled collar or drawdown is withdrawn at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Persons ... may not therefore Deal in the same JB Hi-Fi Securities within any 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor, rolls, partial unwinds and any sale of the collared parcel should be spaced at least six months apart, since each is a Dealing in the same Securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any restriction on Dealing in JB Hi-Fi Securities during a Trading Window which is notified by the Company to all or particular Key Persons or other Employees is a confidential matter which must not be disclosed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The client may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled entry, roll or physical settlement cannot proceed, so the documentation must tolerate silent postponement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only vested and exercisable holdings can be collared; the bank must verify vesting and exercisability before sizing the trade, as there is no approval route for unvested awards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees should ensure that any Securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by: their spouse, partner or child; ... a company or trust over which the Employee has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary) including any self managed superannuation fund.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company does not avoid the approval and disclosure requirements.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no relief for shares under option plans
bespoke_clauses.clause: This may prevent, for example, Key Persons selling, and realising the value of, shares resulting from the exercise of options under a JB Hi-Fi Option Plan at a particular time, even though the Plan rules would otherwise allow this.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the collar out of plan shares can be blocked by a Prohibited Period notwithstanding the plan rules, so cash settlement or a delivery grace period should be provided for.

JBH.summary: A funded collar is achievable for a JB Hi-Fi Director or Executive over vested and exercisable shares, but only with two discretionary approvals and prompt disclosure. The derivative legs require prior written approval of the Relevant Company Officer under section 3.32 because a collar alters the economic benefit or risk derived from JB Hi-Fi Securities (collars are named in the Derivatives definition), and the loan secured on the collared shares requires separate approval under section 3.22 as a 'margin lending or similar funding arrangement'; each approval is valid for 5 trading days, may be refused without reasons and may be revoked before execution. The arrangement must be entered into during one of the three 4 week Trading Windows unless closed-period approval is obtained, must not involve unvested awards (section 3.30 bans hedging these outright, with no exemption), and must not conflict with the ban on Key Persons Dealing in the same Securities within any 6 month period. Both the loan and the hedge must be reported to the Company Secretary (within 24 hours for financing arrangements), are reported periodically to the Board and may be publicly disclosed by JB Hi-Fi even where no law requires it. The policy is silent on forced sales and margin calls, so the documentation should address what happens if enforcement or physical settlement falls in a Closed or confidential Prohibited Period.

Separately, the Company may notify Restricted Persons that they must not trade, either for a specified period or until further notice (s5(b)). The Policy does not say whether such notices are confidential, but a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential (s22).

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named. A purchased put and written call over vested Company securities is an arrangement that operates to limit economic risk and so is a hedging arrangement, which is permitted provided it complies with the rest of the Policy: prior written approval, execution within 7 days, outside blackout periods, and post-trade notification. No venue restriction, so an OTC structure with a bank is covered.
rules.evidence: Any other hedging arrangements involving Company securities must comply with the requirements of this Policy.

rules.detail: Any derivative over unvested Company securities, including equity incentives under the Equity Incentive Plan, that limits economic risk is prohibited outright; there is no approval route.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging unvested securities, extending to securities 'to which they may be entitled', so unvested rights and performance awards are covered as well as issued but unvested shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested securities is expressly permitted but must comply with the Policy: prior written approval from the Chairman (Directors) or CEO or delegate (other Restricted Persons), which may be refused without reasons or granted on conditions, execution within 7 days, no blackout period, satisfaction of the front page test, and prompt notification to the Company Secretary afterwards.
rules.evidence: Any other hedging arrangements involving Company securities must comply with the requirements of this Policy.

rules.detail: The ban bites only on unvested securities. Once plan securities have vested but remain held under the plan, hedging is not prohibited, but any trading in those securities once they cease to be held under the plan must be in accordance with the Policy, so approval and the blackout rules apply.
rules.evidence: where securities in the Company granted under an equity incentive plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any trading in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar with funding or similar structure operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company securities and is therefore a hedging arrangement caught by section 28: prohibited over unvested securities, otherwise permitted subject to approval, blackouts and notification. The substance over form approach in section 2 means the label given to the structure will not determine the analysis.
rules.evidence: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. A short sale would in practice be caught by the ban on speculative or short-term trading in section 25 and by the front page test, but the Policy contains no express short selling prohibition.

Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no definition of trading that would obviously catch a lend and return with no change in beneficial interest; section 34(c) would arguably exclude it as trading with no effective change to the beneficial interest.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities operates to limit or alter economic risk and would be treated as a hedging arrangement requiring compliance with the Policy; in practice a CFD position would also usually offend the ban on speculative or short-term trading in section 25.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted, not prohibited. KMP must obtain approval through the ordinary sections 20 to 24 process, and the Company may impose any conditions it sees fit, expressly including conditions on the circumstances in which Company securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Key management personnel must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in sections 20-24 for any margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending approval requirement sits under the heading 'Additional restrictions applying to key management personnel' and is expressed to apply only to KMP. For a Restricted Person who is not KMP the Policy is silent on margin lending, though any resulting trade in securities would still need approval.
rules.evidence: ADDITIONAL RESTRICTIONS APPLYING TO KEY MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL - MARGIN LENDING ARRANGEMENTS

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, pledge or other security interest over Company securities is not mentioned and is not brought within the description of trading in section 7, which covers buying, selling, agreeing to buy or sell, exercising options, and applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities. The only recognition of an encumbrance is indirect, through the margin lending approval for KMP and the excluded trading carve-out for a secured lender's enforcement sale.

The only secured financing expressly regulated is a 'margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities', which requires approval and may be made conditional. A bank loan secured on collared shares is not named; given the substance over form approach in section 2 it should be treated as within section 32 and approval sought. The Policy positively contemplates secured lending by excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout, approval and short-term rules.
rules.evidence: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 32 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

rules.detail: No defined period; a general prohibition on speculative or short-term trading. Selling shares received on vesting of equity incentive entitlements is expressly not a short-term trade, and section 34 disapplies the prohibition to plan participation, DRP, SPP and rights issue acquisitions, takeover or buy-back disposals, no-change-of-beneficial-interest trades, pre-approved non-discretionary trading plans and secured lender enforcement sales.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval of the collar can be refused purely on perception grounds, independently of inside information or blackouts, and the approver need not give reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a blackout period under section 15, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed trade, obtain written approval for the proposed trade of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no free trading window at all: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement of the collar each need fresh written approval, valid for only 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after the term sheet is agreed but before execution, creating settlement risk for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade Company securities during ... the period from 4.00pm (Sydney time) on 31 March each year until the day following the release to the ASX of the March Quarterly Report.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave short and irregular open periods, so collar entry and any scheduled roll must be timed around four blackouts plus any Board-imposed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only trade securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to trade under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar booked through a spouse, family trust or controlled company must itself be cleared, so the counterparty entity does not avoid the approval requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Sizing must be limited to vested holdings, and the wording 'to which they may be entitled' extends the ban to unvested rights and future entitlements, not just issued shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company has notified the Restricted Persons that they must not trade securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-ended trading ban can be imposed at any time and may block delivery or unwind indefinitely, so the collar documentation needs a settlement deferral mechanism.

WHC.summary: A funded collar is possible for a Whitehaven Director or KMP over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating of the financing leg. The put and call are not named but are hedging arrangements under section 27, which section 28 permits over vested securities provided the Policy is complied with; the loan is regulated only as a 'margin lending arrangement' requiring KMP approval under section 32, and the Company may impose conditions including on when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call. Critically, section 34(e) excludes a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights from the blackout, prior approval and short-term trading rules, so enforcement is not itself a breach. The practical constraints are that every trade, including collar entry, roll and unwind, needs prior written approval that is valid for only 7 days, may be conditioned or revoked at any time and may be refused on front page test grounds, and must fall outside four annual blackouts plus any Board-imposed period; each trade must then be notified to the Company Secretary the same day. Unvested securities, including entitlements the executive may become entitled to, cannot be hedged at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Designated Person wishes to enter an arrangement where Argo securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, they must notify by email the approval group comprising the Chairman, Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar needs only notification, not consent, which is materially easier than the approval regimes in most ASX policies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material, and if required, the Company will disclose the key terms of the arrangement to the market pursuant to the ASX continuous disclosure requirements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The key commercial terms of the facility, potentially including LVR and trigger levels, may be published to the market, so confidentiality cannot be assured to the borrower or the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy does not apply to Designated Persons in the following circumstances: ... Disposal of securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by Argo securities or by the securities of other companies
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An enforcement or margin call sale by the bank is outside the Policy entirely, so it can occur in a prohibited period without breach and needs no clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their Argo security holding must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative legs need email approval from the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary group and must be executed within five trading days and outside prohibited periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company prohibits hedging of unvested Argo securities, such as performance rights awarded under an executive incentive share scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only vested holdings may be collared, and unvested performance rights cannot be counted towards the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All approval requests are to be emailed to the entire approval group, with any one of the group able to grant approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is administratively quick, but approval can also be withdrawn within the five trading day window, creating execution risk before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may from time to time impose additional periods when trading is prohibited, such as ... If it has orders in the market for its own securities due to the activation of an on-market share buy-back or pursuant to any of the Company's employee incentive schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As an LIC that regularly buys back its own shares, Argo can impose additional prohibited periods at short notice, so collar entry, roll and physical settlement dates need flexibility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons also comply with this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances relief is sale only
bespoke_clauses.clause: may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) Argo securities in circumstances otherwise prohibited by this Policy

ARG.summary: A funded collar is workable for an Argo Designated Person over vested shares and this is one of the more permissive policies for the financing leg. The put and call are trading in derivatives over securities and, as an arrangement limiting the economic risk of the holding, need the same approval as a direct trade: an email request to the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary, any one of whom may approve, valid for five trading days unless withdrawn, executed outside the two annual results blackouts and any additional prohibited period, with immediate post-trade report to the Company Secretary. The loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited and requires only email notification to a four-member group including the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, though the Board may treat it as material and disclose its key terms to the market. Enforcement is protected: a disposal by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by Argo securities is excluded from the Policy entirely, so a margin call or default sale in a prohibited period is not a breach and needs no clearance. The only hard prohibition is hedging unvested Argo securities such as unvested performance rights, so the collared parcel must be limited to vested holdings.

VAU.title: Corporate Governance Policies - Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of the Company and its related entities, and where appropriate contractors and consultants. Subject to the basic insider trading restrictions and the absolute ban on hedging unvested shares, options or rights under the employee equity scheme, but not to the closed periods or pre-trade notification regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, all key management personnel as defined in AASB 124, and any other employees, contractors or consultants considered appropriate by the Managing Director and Company Secretary from time to time. Subject to the closed periods, the requirement to notify the Chairman and be advised there is no reason to preclude trading, the short-term trading ban and any Board embargo.

tiers.name: directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company and any of their associates. Restricted Persons who must additionally notify the Company Secretary of any dealings within 5 business days, and who must immediately notify the Chairman or Company Secretary of the details of any hedging of vested options granted under the employee equity scheme.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel as defined in Australian Accounting Standard AASB 124: Related Party Disclosure. Restricted Persons; a senior executive who hedges vested options must immediately notify the Chairman or Company Secretary of the details.

tiers.name: associated parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent or a dependent), family company or trust. Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring associated parties comply with the same restrictions, and the Board may embargo their trading.

rules.section: General - Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme

The only express treatment is that a director or senior executive who enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options under the employee equity scheme must immediately notify the details to the Chairman or Company Secretary. A put and call over vested holdings is therefore not prohibited, but is subject to that notification and, where it involves a trade in the Company's securities, to the closed periods and the pre-trade Chairman notification process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance provision; the only reference is the exclusion of 'a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor subject to approval or notification, and lender enforcement is expressly outside the Policy even in a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: have been advised by the Chairman that there is no reason to preclude them from trading in the Company's securities as notified
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is a discretionary Chairman confirmation with no stated validity period, response time or revocation rule, so the bank should fix its own execution deadline in the term sheet.

bespoke_clauses.clause: have complied with any conditions on trading imposed by the Chairman (including, for example, any time limits applicable to the clearance).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach conditions, including volume or timing limits, that may cut across the hedge ratio or execution schedule agreed with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in the two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports and for 1 business day after the release of the report
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With two week quarterly and four week half and full year blackouts, open windows are short and irregular for a quarterly reporting miner, so entry and roll dates must be planned around them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unqualified embargo can be imposed at any time and extends to family trusts and companies, so it can block collar entry, roll or physical settlement without notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading is a purchase and sale of the same securities within a period between one to six months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any unwind or re-hedge involving the same securities should exceed six months, and there is no carve-out for plan share sales as there is in many policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: closed period relief is sale only
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A closed period unwind requiring a purchase, such as buying back a written call, cannot be cleared even for hardship.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her associated parties (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or facility booked through a family company or trust attracts the same clearance and notification obligations as one in the executive's own name.

bespoke_clauses.clause: arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The notification clause is drafted around vested plan options rather than ordinary shares, so the treatment of a collar over shares held outright rests on the general trading clearance rather than an express permission.

VAU.summary: A funded collar is workable for a Red 5 / Vault Minerals director or senior executive over vested holdings, and the financing leg is essentially unregulated by this policy. Hedging of vested options is expressly permitted subject only to immediate notification of the details to the Chairman or Company Secretary, while hedging or otherwise limiting exposure to risk in unvested shares, options or rights under the employee equity scheme is banned outright for all personnel with no waiver. There is no margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing provision at all, and a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is expressly excluded from the Policy, so a loan secured on the collared shares can be entered and enforced without breaching it. The practical constraints are the pre-trade requirement for a Restricted Person to notify the Chairman and be advised there is no reason to preclude the trade (with any conditions the Chairman imposes, and no stated validity period), the two week quarterly and four week half and full year closed periods, the Board's absolute discretion to impose an embargo at any time, and the ban on Restricted Persons buying and selling the same securities within one to six months. Directors must also notify the Company Secretary of any dealing within 5 business days.

The Company may also notify Employees that they must not deal in securities, either for a specified period or until further notice (s4.1). The Policy does not state whether these notices are confidential, but a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential (s6(c)).

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named or defined. A purchased put and written call over vested, unrestricted Company securities is an arrangement that operates to limit economic risk and so is hedging; the Policy prohibits hedging only of unvested plan securities and securities under a holding lock, so hedging vested holdings is permitted, subject to prior written approval under section 5.1 (valid 5 business days), the blackout periods and the Front Page Test. No venue limitation.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Any derivative that limits the economic risk of unvested plan securities is prohibited absolutely; the word 'never' leaves no approval or exceptional circumstances route.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired by a Restricted Person under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under a plan may never be hedged, so vested shares still inside a plan holding lock cannot form part of the collared parcel.
rules.evidence: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging plan securities before vesting.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired by a Restricted Person under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban while the securities are subject to a holding lock or a restriction on dealing under the terms of a Company equity plan.
rules.evidence: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Section 5.4 defines hedging and then prohibits it only in the two stated cases, so hedging vested and unrestricted holdings is permitted. It is a dealing requiring prior approval on the Clearance to Trade Request Form, which may be refused without reasons, made subject to conditions or revoked at any time, must be executed within 5 business days, must fall outside the blackouts and must satisfy the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The hedging restrictions sit in section 5 (Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons) and do not apply to Employees who are not Restricted Persons; for them only the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test and the blackout periods apply.

Monetisation is not named. A collar with a loan, prepaid forward or similar structure limits the economic risk of holding Company securities and so is hedging: permitted over vested unrestricted holdings with approval, prohibited over unvested or holding-locked plan securities. Forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a short-term dealing, so a short-dated monetisation risks breaching section 5.3, and the substance over form principle in section 1 means labels will not control the analysis.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is expressly named as a form of prohibited speculative dealing, with no approval route. This does not on its face catch a covered hedge over shares actually held, but any naked short leg of a structure would be prohibited.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending by a holder is not mentioned; borrowing appears only in the description of short selling in section 5.3. A lend and return would arguably fall within the excluded dealing for dealings with no effective change to the beneficial interest.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities that limits the economic risk of a holding is hedging and so is permitted over vested unrestricted holdings with approval and prohibited over unvested or holding-locked plan securities; in practice a CFD position would usually be caught by the ban on speculative or short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition with no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances route and no security-state or tier carve-out within Restricted Persons. Given the substance over form principle, a loan secured on Company shares with margin call or LVR mechanics is likely to be treated as a margin lending arrangement in relation to the Company's securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending prohibition sits under 'Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons' and is expressed to bind Restricted Persons only; the Policy says nothing about margin lending by other Employees.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, pledge or other security interest over Company securities is not mentioned and is not brought within the description of dealing in section 3, which covers buying, selling, agreeing to buy or sell, exercising options and applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities. The only recognition of a security interest is the excluded dealing for a secured lender's enforcement sale.

The only financing arrangement expressly regulated is a margin lending arrangement, which is prohibited. Secured financing generally is not addressed: there is no approval, notification or disclosure requirement for a loan secured on Company securities, and section 7(g) contemplates that secured lending may exist by excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval rules. Whether a bank facility secured on collared shares is caught depends on whether it is characterised as a margin lending arrangement, which the substance over form principle makes likely where it has margin call features.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.

rules.detail: Buying and selling on market within a 90 day period is prohibited, as is entering into other short term dealings, with forward contracts given as the example. Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 90 days of the vesting date is expressly not a short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

DNL.exemption_authority: Section 4.5: an Employee who needs to deal during a blackout period because of exceptional circumstances, likely severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and who holds no Inside Information, may apply for approval through the section 6 process; approval is granted only on sufficient evidence, in the clearer's opinion, that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. Approval will never be granted where the dealing fails the Front Page Test (s4.2). There is no power to exempt anyone from the margin lending prohibition or the hedging prohibitions in section 5.4.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is the problem: if the facility secured on the collared shares is characterised as a margin lending arrangement it is flatly prohibited for Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A facility documented as a term loan rather than a margin loan will still be assessed on its substance, so LVR tests, top-up rights and enforcement over the shares make the section 5.2 ban likely to bite.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or forward leg can itself be a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed 90 days and early termination rights should be limited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough: shares still under a plan holding lock cannot be collared, so the bank must diligence lock status as well as vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.3, 4.4 and 5.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a compliant secured facility could be put in place, enforcement sales sit outside the blackout and approval rules, though this carve-out cannot cure the margin lending prohibition itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an otherwise compliant collar over vested shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, and the approver need not give reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no free trading window: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement each need fresh written approval, valid only 5 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after pricing is agreed and the client cannot explain why, so the documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal before settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not deal in Company securities: from the close of trading on the ASX on 30 September each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the full year results ... from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the half-year results.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The blackouts follow a 30 September financial year end, and approval is described as more likely only in the 4 weeks after each results release, so execution should be scheduled into those windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the structure through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the margin lending ban or the clearance requirement.

DNL.summary: The derivative legs of a collar are achievable for a Restricted Person, but the funding leg is the obstacle. Hedging is defined as any arrangement limiting the economic risk of holding Company securities and is prohibited only over unvested plan securities and securities under a plan holding lock, so a put and call over vested, unrestricted shares is permitted subject to prior written approval on the Clearance to Trade Request Form (Chairman for Directors, Company Secretary for Senior Executives), execution within 5 business days, the 30 September and 31 March blackouts and the Front Page Test. However, section 5.2 flatly prohibits Restricted Persons from entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities, with no approval route, and the express substance over form principle means a bank facility secured on the collared shares with LVR or margin call mechanics is likely to be treated as such, so a funded structure would need to be demonstrably not a margin lending arrangement. Tenor is a further constraint: forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a prohibited short term dealing and buying and selling within 90 days is banned, so the collar should run well beyond 90 days. If a compliant facility could be structured, section 7(g) helpfully excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval rules.
